## Yhidrous worshippers traits

### Boons - Fiendish Worship

#### Evangelist
**1: Consumption of the Worm (Sp)** _corrosive touch_ 3/day, _acid arrow_ 2/day, or _vampiric touch_ 1/day
**2: Nightmare Below (Ex and Su)** You can crawl beneath the surface of the earth like a worm and then burst forth to horrify foes. You gain a burrow speed of 30 feet, which can be used only in mud, sand, soil, or other soft substances (not solid stone). You gain a +10 bonus on Stealth checks while burrowing. Once per hour, if you take a standard action to emerge from burrowing with a roar and spray of soil, each creature within 30 feet of your emergence that was not aware of your presence must succeed at a Will save (DC = 10 + half your Hit Dice + your Charisma modifier) or be shaken and stunned for 1 round and shaken for 2d4 rounds thereafter. The burrowing ability is an extraordinary ability, but the latter part of the ability is a supernatural, mind-affecting fear effect.
**3: The Very Worm That Gnaws (Su)** As a result of your practice of sleeping in parasite-infested mud or soil to fulfill your obedience to Yhidothrus, your flesh has become riddled with an unholy infection. Yet far from being a troublesome condition, these worms are a welcome addition to your life, and as you gain this final boon, your body is devoured from the inside out by a mass of wriggling leeches, maggots, worms, and other horrid vermin, which are thereafter bound together into a cohesive whole by your foul will. When you attain this boon, you become a worm that walks. When your emergence (see above) causes creatures to become shaken, those creatures are also sickened for 1 minute.

#### Exalted
**1: Blessing of the Worm (Sp)** _ray of enfeeblement_ 3/day, _gentle repose_ 2/day, or _slow_ 1/day
**2: Curse of Brittle Bones (Sp)** Once per day, you can cast a powerful _bestow curse_, heightened to a 7th-level spell, as a spell-like ability. This special curse causes the target creature to suddenly advance to venerable age. This curse imposes a –6 penalty to the target’s Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores, but its Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma scores do not increase. These penalties do not stack with any existing penalties a creature might already have as the result of advanced age.
**3: Call of the Worm (Sp)** By placing a hand upon the ground and whispering a series of blasphemies to the Ravager Worm, you can call up from below an immense and destructive manifestation of your fiendish lord. You can cast _summon monster IX_ once per day as a spell-like ability to summon one advanced fiendish purple worm.

#### Sentinel
**1: Hasten the End (Sp)** _expeditious retreat_ 3/day, _silence_ 2/day, or _sands of time_ 1/day
**2: Specter of Time (Su)** As a swift action when you confirm a critical hit with a weapon against a living foe, instead of dealing the additional damage from the critical hit, you can instead deal normal damage and force the target to attempt a Fortitude save (DC = 10 + half your Hit Dice + your Charisma modifier). On a failed save, the target painfully advances in years to the next age category. This aging can never have beneficial effects (such as if used against a true dragon). The target gains the penalties associated with the new age category to its Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores, but its Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma scores do not increase. This advanced age effect lasts for 24 hours before it fades and the affected creature returns to its normal age. A venerable creature (including one whose age has been magically accelerated via this ability to venerable, but not one whose age is temporarily advanced from other effects, such as per _sands of time_) that fails its saving throw against the aging effects of this ability is instantly slain, as if via old age (though the body instantly reverts to its original age appearance upon death). A creature slain by this effect can only be restored to life via _miracle_, _reincarnate_, _true resurrection_, or _wish_. This is a curse effect.
**3: End Time (Sp)** You can call upon the Ravager Worm to temporarily consume time itself in an area surrounding you. You can cast _time stop_ once per day as a spell-like ability. When you use this ability, those in the area of effect are subjected to a powerful vision—that the world they are in becomes wrapped in the endless coils of the Ravager Worm. The affected creatures never glimpse Yhidothrus’s head, and know only for the brief instant of eternity they spend in your time stop area that the world around them is fully wrapped in the coils of something more foul than they even imagined.

name: Cragback
summary: Rock-backed beast of Ordon and Hjarthland: territorial in the wild, a prized pack animal when domesticated.

fields.habitat: Mountains, rocky highlands and trade routes
fields.temperament: Aggressive when wild, dependable when domesticated

body:
**Cragbacks** are heavy, rock-backed beasts found in [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md) and Hjarthland. In the wild they are territorial and dangerous, but when properly domesticated they are widely used as pack animals.

They are especially valued for hauling supplies through steep, broken or snowy terrain.

## Appearance

Cragbacks are broad, low-bodied animals with thick limbs and dense hides. Their backs naturally grow stony ridges and mineral formations, giving them the appearance of walking hills.

Some individuals also develop bright crystalline growths, especially in older specimens.

## Behaviour

Wild Cragbacks are short-tempered and highly defensive. They charge intruders, especially if startled or cornered.

Domesticated Cragbacks have been trained to be more dependable, but are still known for their temper. They can carry heavy loads across mountains, mines and winter roads with little complaint.

## Use as Pack Animals

Cragbacks are prized in both Ordon and Hjarthland because they can travel where wheeled transport struggles.

Ordonian merchants and miners use them in rocky uplands and industrial routes, while Hjarthland communities rely on them to move goods through snow and uneven ground.

Their broad backs and natural sturdiness make them ideal beasts of burden.

## Rock Growths

The formations on a Cragback's back continue growing throughout its life.

These growths can be:

- Bare stone ridges
- Mineral plates
- Crystal clusters
- Moss-covered crags

Handlers sometimes trim or shape these formations to make it easier to fasten cargo.

## Challenge Rating

Cragbacks have a **Challenge Rating of 1**.

A domesticated Cragback is usually docile, but a wild one is dangerous due to its size, aggression and ability to trample or gore attackers.

name: Driftling
summary: Small, lazy, loyal semi-aquatic mammal that floats downstream on its back through the rivers of four regions.

fields.habitat: Rivers, lakes, estuaries and sheltered coastlines
fields.diet: Fish, shellfish, aquatic plants and discarded food

body:
**Driftlings** are small semi-aquatic mammals found throughout the rivers, lakes and sheltered coastlines of [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md), Shinkira, Hjarthland and Nareth.

They are named for their habit of floating on their backs and allowing rivers to carry them downstream.

Driftlings are famously lazy, but form strong and lasting bonds with their families, companions and human caretakers.

“Never ask a Driftling where it's going.

It probably doesn't know either.”

— Common riverside saying

## Appearance

Driftlings have rounded bodies, short limbs, broad tails and thick water-resistant fur. Their large eyes allow them to see effectively in dark or murky water.

Their coat colours vary between brown, cream, grey and pale gold.

Regional populations have developed minor differences suited to their environments.

**Natural swimmers**

Despite their small limbs and relaxed appearance, Driftlings are extremely capable swimmers.

Their broad tails provide most of their propulsion, allowing them to move considerably faster in water than on land.

## Behaviour

Driftlings spend much of their lives sleeping, eating or drifting with the current.

Although they are capable swimmers, they avoid unnecessary effort. A Driftling travelling downstream may float for several miles without deliberately choosing a destination.

Groups often sleep close together in calm water.

They may hold paws, tails or pieces of floating vegetation to prevent themselves from drifting apart.

Driftlings are highly social. Once one has bonded with a person or another animal, it may remain loyal to them for the rest of its life.

They are also notably reluctant to leave comfortable sleeping locations.

Attempts to move a sleeping Driftling often result in the animal immediately returning to the same location.

## Habitat and Range

Driftlings favour slow-moving rivers, sheltered lakes, estuaries and coastlines with plentiful food.

They are considered a [widespread Kurovian species](/content/lore/creatures.md) because healthy populations exist in several otherwise very different regions.

They adapt particularly well to waterways altered by human settlement.

Canals, docks, artificial ponds and reservoirs may all support Driftling populations.

## Regional Populations

### [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md)

**Ordonian Driftlings** are commonly found in canals, freight rivers and industrial docks.

Many have learned to climb aboard barges and simply allow themselves to be carried between settlements.

Dockworkers often consider them good-luck animals, despite their habit of sleeping inside unattended cargo.

Some individual Driftlings become so familiar with particular trade routes that crews recognise them on sight.

### Shinkira

**Shinkiran Driftlings** commonly possess lighter beige or cream-coloured coats.

They favour irrigation channels, quiet riverbanks and ponds close to human settlement.

Driftlings living around agricultural communities frequently become semi-tame, returning to the same houses or farms when food is available.

Some rural families consider a Driftling repeatedly visiting the same home a sign of good fortune.

### Hjarthland

**Hjarthland Driftlings** have especially thick coats and can survive in water which would be dangerous to most similar animals.

They are often allowed into homes during severe winter storms.

Refusing shelter to a Driftling is considered needlessly cruel in many Hjarthland communities.

Allowing one inside without securing the pantry is considered needlessly foolish.

### Nareth

**Narethian Driftlings** inhabit rivers, swamps and flooded rainforests.

They are generally more alert than populations elsewhere due to the region's numerous predators.

Rather than sleeping in open water, they often rest among roots, reeds or upon the backs of sufficiently large and slow-moving creatures.

The latter behaviour appears to irritate the animals being used as resting places considerably more than it concerns the Driftling.

## Relationship with People

Driftlings are commonly kept as pets and shipboard mascots.

They are particularly popular among fishermen, bargemen and communities living near rivers.

They can be trained to retrieve objects and locate familiar people, but make poor conventional working animals.

A Driftling usually performs a task only when motivated by:

- food;
- affection;
- curiosity;
- or concern for a bonded companion.

Their fondness for food can make them a nuisance around markets, docks and kitchens.

A Driftling which learns where food is stored is remarkably difficult to convince that it should not return.

**Domestication**

Driftlings are considered partially domesticated in several regions.

However, the distinction between a domestic Driftling and a wild Driftling which has discovered free food is frequently unclear.

## Hunting and Pelts

Driftling fur is dense, soft and naturally resistant to water.

It is traditionally used for waterproof clothing, winter garments, gloves and expensive coat linings.

The value of their pelts has led to organised hunting in parts of [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md) and Hjarthland.

This practice is controversial because Driftlings are social, intelligent and often unafraid of people.

Hunters can exploit their trusting behaviour to approach them easily.

Some riverside settlements have banned Driftling hunting, while others permit it only during particular seasons.

Several regions have increasingly moved toward obtaining Driftling fur through brushing and grooming domesticated animals rather than killing them.

## Challenge Rating

Driftlings have a **Challenge Rating of 1/8**.

They are not naturally aggressive and normally escape danger by swimming or hiding.

When cornered, injured or defending a bonded companion, a Driftling may bite and scratch.

Their threat comes primarily from their speed in water and determination rather than physical strength.

## Adventure Uses

A Driftling could appear as:

- A missing pet belonging to an important NPC
- A barge or ship mascot
- A guide to something hidden beneath a river
- A creature carrying evidence tangled in its fur
- The target of illegal pelt hunters
- The only surviving animal from a contaminated waterway
- A loyal companion searching for its missing owner
- An Utsuro-altered Driftling developing an unusual ability

> If one is asleep in your boat, it is probably too late to argue about ownership.

name: Dustkip
summary: Harmless yellow-scaled desert creature of Halingo, often kept as a pet; 'alive as a Dustkip' means a survivor.
body:
**Dustkips** are small desert creatures native to [Halingo](/content/locations/halingo.md). They are harmless, resourceful and capable of surviving in conditions that would kill many larger animals.

Wild Dustkips are commonly found near rocks, abandoned machinery and the outskirts of settlements. Some are kept as household pets.

## Appearance

Dustkips are small, yellow-scaled creatures with rounded bodies, large eyes and thick tails.

Their colouring helps them blend into Halingo's sand and dry grass. Dustkips living near the Black Sea often develop darker patches from soot and industrial waste.

## Survival

Dustkips possess no meaningful combat abilities. They survive by avoiding danger rather than confronting it.

They can burrow into cool sand, find small sources of water and eating roots, insects and scraps. Their thick tails store fat and moisture, allowing them to survive several days without food or water.

The Halingan phrase **“alive as a Dustkip”** is used for someone who survives circumstances that should have killed them.

## Behaviour

Dustkips are cautious but naturally curious. They often observe travellers from behind rocks before slowly approaching in search of food.

When frightened, a Dustkip freezes, flattens itself against the ground or disappears into the nearest available gap.

They communicate through soft chirps, tail movements and rapid blinking.

## Relationship with People

Dustkips are sometimes kept as pets in Halingan settlements.

They are inexpensive to feed, tolerate extreme heat and quickly become affectionate toward people who treat them kindly. A domesticated Dustkip often sleeps inside boots, cupboards or piles of clothing.

## Challenge Rating

Dustkips have a **Challenge Rating of 0**.

They cannot effectively harm most creatures and will always attempt to flee or hide when threatened.

name: Elyrra
summary: The Mother of Strangers: an Umbuso whose touch makes living organisms grow other, unrelated life.
body:
> **DIRECT CONTACT WITH UMB-052 IS PROHIBITED.**
>
> Any organism touched by UMB-052 must be treated as an active biological hazard regardless of apparent condition.
>
> Secondary organisms produced following exposure are **not** to be assumed harmless.

*Sanitised reconstruction of UMB-052. Individual manifestations display substantial anatomical variation.*

**Elyrra**, commonly titled **the Mother of Strangers**, is an [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md) whose physical contact causes uncontrolled biological growth within living organisms.

The resulting life does not need to correspond to the species of the affected organism.

Documented growths include fungi, additional organs, limbs, eyes, teeth, parasitic organisms and complete animals.

Some remain alive after removal.

## Overview

UMB-052 possesses an irregular body composed of eyes, mouths, tendrils and brightly coloured organic structures.

No stable anatomy has been established.

The entity's primary anomalous property occurs through physical contact.

Affected organisms undergo a process formally designated **Heterologous Proliferation**.

Elyrra does not cause organisms to reproduce.

It causes them to grow **other life**.

The process may begin within minutes or remain dormant for several days.

No reliable method exists for determining which tissue will develop.

## Heterologous Proliferation

Post-exposure growth varies drastically between subjects.

Recorded examples include:

- fungal colonies growing beneath human skin;
- additional eyes developing upon livestock;
- fully formed teeth appearing inside muscle tissue;
- plant structures growing from animals;
- independent worm-like organisms budding from limbs;
- duplicate organs with incompatible anatomy;
- and small vertebrates developing externally from hosts belonging to unrelated species.

Genetic analysis has produced inconsistent results.

Some growths correspond to known species.

Others contain characteristics from several unrelated organisms.

A significant number match **nothing currently catalogued**.

**UMB-052 TEST SUBJECT 14**

HOST: Caprine animal

INITIAL EXPOSURE: Left shoulder

+4 HOURS: Local swelling

+11 HOURS: Visible structures beneath skin

+19 HOURS: ██████████████████

+23 HOURS: Three organisms separated from host

HOST SURVIVAL: NO

OFFSPRING SURVIVAL: **YES**

## Anatomy

Elyrra's visible body contains an extraordinary concentration of sensory structures.

Numerous eyes of varying sizes and colours appear across the surface.

Mouths occur without obvious digestive organisation.

Structures resembling:

- feathers;
- fur;
- roots;
- fungal growth;
- tentacles;
- cartilage;
- exposed nerves;
- and flowering tissue

have all been documented.

Whether these structures constitute Elyrra's natural anatomy is unknown.

One hypothesis proposes that much of its visible body consists of organisms produced by previous contact with itself.

This has not been verified.

## Behaviour

Elyrra does not display consistent predatory behaviour.

It nevertheless makes frequent physical contact with its surroundings.

Whether this is deliberate is disputed.

The entity has been observed brushing against vegetation, animals and structures without pausing.

Affected organisms may remain apparently normal after Elyrra has moved on.

This makes post-manifestation contamination considerably more dangerous than the initial encounter.

The disappearance of UMB-052 does not end an UMB-052 incident.

In most cases, it marks the beginning.

## Incident UMB-052-19

Following a confirmed manifestation, authorities located twelve exposed animals.

All were isolated.

Over the next four days, biological growth was detected throughout the surrounding area.

No additional contact with Elyrra had occurred.

Investigators subsequently identified:

**12** confirmed exposed animals.

**37** secondary organisms.

**114** tertiary biological anomalies.

████████████████████████████████████████████████████

The concept of **tertiary exposure** was introduced following this incident.

The mechanism remains disputed.

## Current Status

UMB-052 is classified:

**ACTIVE — UNLOCATED**

No confirmed manifestation is currently under observation.

Biological material associated with previous incidents remains in containment.

The oldest surviving Elyrran Growth is currently ██ years old.

It remains alive.

Its original host died within fourteen hours.

**ENCOUNTER GUIDANCE // UMB-052**

**DO NOT TOUCH UMB-052.**

**DO NOT ALLOW UMB-052 TO TOUCH YOU.**

Avoid contact with organisms, vegetation or biological material present along its route.

Following suspected exposure, isolate immediately.

Do not attempt to cut away unexplained growth without medical containment.

If a newly developed structure begins moving independently:

DO NOT REMOVE IT YOURSELF.

> Life follows where she touches.
> It does not follow correctly.
>
> — Early UMB-052 field report

name: Hoshikui
summary: The Star-Eater: a lost Shinkiran Umbuso, a vast black shape trailing yellow lights, remembered in village warnings.

fields.habitat: Mountain valleys, agricultural regions, old shrines and isolated settlements
fields.first_record: Unknown; references predate surviving Shinkiran records

body:
*A depiction of Hoshikui overlooking an isolated settlement in rural Shinkira.*

**Hoshikui**, commonly translated as the **Star-Eater**, is one of the [Hundred Gods](/content/lore/umbuso.md) and an exceptionally rare [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md) associated with the remote countryside of Shinkira.

It is regarded by most modern Shinkirans as a creature of folklore. In villages where traditions surrounding Hoshikui have survived, however, stories concerning the creature are treated less as legends and more as instructions.

## Overview

Unlike more commonly encountered Umbuso, Hoshikui is not believed to represent a species. Every surviving account appears to describe the same entity.

Historical records describe an enormous black creature bearing vast membranous appendages and a trail of brilliant yellow lights stretching from its head along its spine and tail.

The origin and function of these lights remain unknown.

Hoshikui is listed among the [Hundred Gods](/content/lore/umbuso.md) because references to it appear in traditions considerably older than most surviving accounts of human resistance against the Umbuso.

Its apparent disappearance led scholars to classify the creature as **lost**.

Reports from rural Shinkira suggest that classification may be premature.

## Appearance

Hoshikui possesses an enormous and poorly defined body which absorbs almost all visible detail.

Its silhouette has been variously compared to a dragon, a malformed quadruped and an enormous mass of roots or hanging fabric.

Numerous tendril-like structures descend from its head, torso and limbs.

Two vast membranes rise from the upper body. They are usually referred to as wings, although no reliable account describes Hoshikui using them for flight.

The creature's defining characteristic is a chain of luminous yellow structures scattered across its head, spine and tail.

Some resemble tiny lights.

Others resemble four-pointed stars.

The largest appear as brilliant circular masses.

Despite their brightness, they seemingly cast almost no light upon Hoshikui itself.

The creature remains a silhouette even while surrounded by them.

## Behaviour

## Folklore

Rural Shinkiran folklore places particular importance upon the lights covering Hoshikui.

One tradition claims that each represents something consumed by the creature.

A small light represents a person.

A larger light represents a family.

A star represents an entire settlement.

No evidence exists to support this interpretation.

Another tradition claims the lights are stars removed from the night sky and carried permanently upon Hoshikui's body.

The creature's common name, **Star-Eater**, originates from this belief.

Children in several isolated Shinkiran communities are still taught a traditional warning:

*One light is nothing.*

 

*Two lights are watching.*

 

*Three lights know your name.*

 

*If the whole sky walks, close the door.*

## Encounters

Almost every credible modern report originates from rural Shinkira.

Sightings are particularly associated with terraced farmland, mountain valleys, forest roads and settlements containing shrines significantly older than the communities surrounding them.

Witnesses who remain inside buildings are substantially more likely to survive an encounter.

Individuals who attempt to approach the creature frequently disappear.

There are no confirmed records of Hoshikui being killed.

Several historical accounts describe attacks using conventional weapons or Axius.

None record a successful injury.

**Encounter Guidance**

If Hoshikui is suspected to be nearby, remain within a building and do not attempt to observe it from close range.

Do not approach lights appearing in fields, forests or mountains.

Do not attempt to count the lights upon the creature.

Do not respond to unexplained voices outside the settlement.

Most importantly:

**Never follow the lights.**

## Relationship with Axius

## Notes

A recurring connection exists between Hoshikui sightings and extremely old rural shrines.

Many of these structures have no surviving religious affiliation.

Local communities continue maintaining them despite no longer knowing which god, spirit or ancestor they originally honoured.

Some scholars studying the [Hundred Gods](/content/lore/umbuso.md) have suggested these structures may never have been places of worship.

They may instead have been **boundary markers**.

Several surviving inscriptions associated with such shrines contain variations of the same phrase:

*Do not follow the lights.*

Whether these structures repel Hoshikui or simply mark locations where the creature has previously appeared remains unknown.

> If the stars descend below the mountains, shut the doors. If they begin to move, do not look again.
>
> — Traditional Shinkiran warning

name: Kharuun
summary: Faceless, crystal-armoured aberration of Targoth that distorts weight around itself, lifting stones before bringing them crashing down.

fields.habitat: Mountains, crater fields and rocky wastes

body:
**Kharuun** are rare quadrupedal Aberrations found exclusively in Targoth.

They possess heavily armoured bodies, enormous crescent horns and a completely featureless head lacking eyes, nostrils or a visible mouth.

Kharuun are particularly feared for their ability to distort weight around themselves, lifting loose stone and debris from the ground before violently bringing it back down.

**DANGER — CR 8**

Kharuun are highly territorial and capable of crushing mounted travellers or breaking through light fortifications during a charge.

Do not mistake the absence of eyes for blindness.

## Appearance

Adult Kharuun are heavily built creatures covered in pale coarse fur and dense black crystalline armour.

Their most recognisable features are two enormous violet-black horns curving around an otherwise featureless head.

No eyes, nostrils, mouth or conventional ears have been identified.

The tail is long and segmented, terminating in irregular crystalline growths which continue developing throughout the creature's life.

Small fragments occasionally break away without apparent injury.

**Anatomical anomaly**

Dissections have located neither a conventional mouth nor a digestive tract capable of sustaining an animal of this size.

How Kharuun obtain nourishment remains unresolved.

## Spatial Distortion

Kharuun tissue contains unusually dense concentrations of Axius, particularly around the horns and crystalline growths.

When threatened, an adult can create a short-lived distortion in the area surrounding itself.

Recorded effects include:

- loose stones rising from the ground;
- sudden changes in perceived weight;
- people and animals being pulled off balance;
- projectiles changing trajectory;
- fragments of rock orbiting the creature;
- and suspended debris crashing violently back to the ground.

The phenomenon ordinarily lasts only a few seconds.

The stones rising are the warning.

Do not wait for them to reach their highest point.

Some researchers believe the Kharuun is manipulating gravity.

Others argue that the effect represents an unusual manifestation of Axius rather than gravity itself.

Neither explanation has been conclusively demonstrated.

## Senses

Kharuun possess no visible eyes or ears.

Experiments suggest that they detect movement through ground vibration, changes in air pressure and fluctuations in surrounding Axius.

This does not fully explain their awareness.

Kharuun have accurately located stationary individuals at distances where neither vibration nor sound should have provided sufficient information.

Attempts to blind or visually distract a Kharuun are therefore ineffective.

## Habitat

Kharuun are found exclusively within Targoth.

They favour:

- high mountain valleys;
- exposed rocky plains;
- ancient crater fields;
- abandoned settlements;
- and the barren country surrounding Mount Targon.

Known territories frequently contain unusual quantities of dark crystalline material.

Whether the Kharuun seek these deposits, feed upon them, or somehow produce them remains disputed.

Sightings become considerably more frequent closer to Mount Targon.

## Crystalline Growths

The black structures covering a Kharuun are neither ordinary stone nor conventional biological armour.

They grow directly from underlying tissue and contain unusually high concentrations of Axius.

Damaged formations slowly regenerate.

Larger crystals are particularly common along the back, forelimbs and tail.

Material recovered from dead specimens may retain weak spatial effects for several hours.

Older fragments eventually become inert.

This material is highly valuable to researchers, although transporting freshly recovered samples requires specialised containment.

## Challenge Rating

**Threat: Severe**

Kharuun combine heavy natural armour, tremendous charging power and short-range spatial distortion.

Their most dangerous attacks are usually preceded by nearby stones and debris beginning to rise.

Experienced parties are advised to remain mobile and avoid fighting on unstable terrain.

## Adventure Uses

A Kharuun may appear as:

- a creature blocking an important mountain pass;
- the inhabitant of a newly discovered crater;
- the reason a mining settlement was abandoned;
- the source of unexplained gravitational disturbances;
- a specimen sought by researchers studying Aberrations;
- a territorial creature disturbed by excavation near Mount Targon;
- or evidence that something beneath Targoth is affecting the surrounding wildlife.

> When the rocks begin to float, leave.

name: Kharvassa
summary: The Mother Below: an immense subterranean Umbuso beneath Halingo's deep desert, mother of the Sandwyrms.
body:
*Reconstruction of UMB-028 emerging from the deep sands of [Halingo](/content/locations/halingo.md). Scale approximate.*

**Kharvassa**, commonly titled **the Mother Below**, is an [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md) believed to inhabit the deepest desert regions of [Halingo](/content/locations/halingo.md).

The entity bears a strong anatomical resemblance to the numerous species collectively referred to as Sandwyrms, though on a scale unmatched by any confirmed specimen.

Historical tradition identifies Kharvassa as the **mother of the Sandwyrms**.

For centuries this was regarded as mythology.

Modern biological evidence has made the distinction considerably less comfortable.

**ARCHIVAL SUMMARY**

UMB-028 is not to be approached for reproductive study.

UMB-028 is not to be sampled.

Sandwyrms observed travelling toward a suspected UMB-028 location are not to be followed.

Previous exemptions to these rules have been revoked.

## Overview

Kharvassa is an immense subterranean organism associated with the deserts of [Halingo](/content/locations/halingo.md).

Most of its body remains beneath the sand.

The visible organism consists of a vast central mass from which numerous serpentine necks emerge, each terminating in an independent jaw.

The exact number of heads is disputed.

Reports have documented between seven and thirteen simultaneously.

No complete view of the body has ever been recorded.

Unlike many Umbuso, Kharvassa appears to have a clear ecological relationship with a widespread group of lesser organisms.

Those organisms are the Sandwyrms of Halingo.

Every Sandwyrm tested in Halingo has contained genetic material which does not belong to the Sandwyrm.

The unidentified material is identical between specimens.

The source of this material is presently classified as **UMB-028-compatible**.

## Appearance

Kharvassa possesses an enormous dark body resembling a partially buried mass of overlapping serpentine organisms.

Several long necks rise independently from the central body.

Each terminates in an elongated jaw lined with numerous pale teeth.

No eyes have been identified.

The necks appear capable of acting independently and have been observed:

- investigating separate targets;
- consuming different organisms simultaneously;
- responding independently to sound;
- retreating beneath the sand individually;
- and displaying apparently conflicting behaviour.

Whether the heads possess independent nervous systems is unknown.

The central body has never been excavated.

Ground-penetrating surveys indicate that the visible portion constitutes only a small fraction of the organism.

How small remains disputed.

## Sandwyrms

Numerous species of Sandwyrm inhabit Halingo.

Until relatively recently, their resemblance to Kharvassa was considered an example of regional folklore influencing natural history.

This changed following genetic analysis of tissue recovered from three unrelated Sandwyrm species.

All three contained the same unidentified sequence.

Further testing found it throughout Halingo's Sandwyrm population.

The sequence is absent from Sandwyrms collected outside the region.

**HALINGO SANDWYRM SPECIES TESTED:** 17

**SPECIES CONTAINING SEQUENCE UMB-028-A:** 17

**KNOWN NON-HALINGO SPECIES CONTAINING SEQUENCE:** 0

**SOURCE ORGANISM:** PRESUMED UMB-028

Kharvassa may therefore be:

- the direct ancestor of Halingo's Sandwyrms;
- a parent organism which continues producing them;
- an organism capable of altering existing Sandwyrm populations;
- or something for which conventional concepts of ancestry are inadequate.

The common title **Mother Below** predates this discovery by several centuries.

## Reproduction

No confirmed Sandwyrm birth has ever been observed in proximity to Kharvassa.

No eggs have been recovered.

No reproductive organs have been identified.

Nevertheless, increases in Sandwyrm activity frequently follow suspected UMB-028 manifestations.

The most significant event occurred after the ████████ Tremor.

For twelve days, Sandwyrms emerged from approximately 140 kilometres of desert surrounding the suspected location of Kharvassa.

The organisms did not attack nearby settlements.

Instead, they travelled toward a single point.

**OBSERVATION DAY 4**

Wyrms continue entering Zone 3.

None have been observed leaving.

Acoustic monitoring suggests movement beneath us considerably exceeds the number entering from the surface.

Request to relocate monitoring station denied.

**OBSERVATION DAY 5**

Request repeated.

**OBSERVATION DAY 6**

██████████████████████████████████████████████

The observation station was abandoned shortly afterward.

Sandwyrm numbers throughout western Halingo increased sharply over the following three years.

## The Brood Call

Sandwyrms appear capable of detecting Kharvassa across extraordinary distances.

Prior to suspected awakenings, local populations exhibit a behaviour known as the **Brood Call**.

The Sandwyrms stop hunting.

Individuals abandon established territories.

Migration begins toward a shared destination.

Species which ordinarily attack one another travel alongside each other without conflict.

During major events, hundreds may move simultaneously.

When the Sandwyrms stop eating, leave.

They have found something more important than hunger.

The mechanism responsible for this behaviour has not been identified.

No audible call has been detected.

Axius monitoring produces inconsistent results.

## Behaviour

Kharvassa spends the majority of its known existence beneath the desert.

Periods of surface activity are rare.

When active, individual heads may emerge across an area spanning several kilometres.

Early explorers therefore occasionally recorded separate creatures without realising they belonged to the same organism.

The heads demonstrate aggressive feeding behaviour toward large animals and unfamiliar movement.

Human beings are not specifically targeted.

This distinction provides little practical protection.

Kharvassa has consumed:

- caravans;
- livestock herds;
- military vehicles;
- Sandwyrms;
- structures;
- and sections of exposed rock.

The function of this feeding is unknown.

No corresponding increase in body mass has been measured.

## Beneath Halingo

The greatest uncertainty surrounding Kharvassa concerns its actual size.

Surface sightings occur across locations separated by distances too great to reasonably belong to a single conventional organism.

Two explanations dominate current research.

The first proposes that multiple Kharvassa-class organisms exist.

The second proposes that all known sightings represent a single subterranean body.

The latter was once considered biologically impossible.

Subsurface mapping conducted in ████ detected a continuous structure beneath several confirmed manifestation sites.

The survey was repeated.

The structure remained.

Its dimensions were removed from the public report.

██████████████████████████████████████████████████████

**INTERNAL MEMORANDUM**

Stop referring to UMB-028 as being *beneath the Halingo desert*.

Following Survey 12, this terminology is misleading.

████████████████████████████████████████████

## Settlements

Several ancient Halingo settlements were built upon elevated stone formations despite nearby access to substantially more hospitable terrain.

Local traditions typically attribute this to protection from Sandwyrms.

Archaeological evidence suggests another purpose.

Many settlements were positioned specifically outside zones associated with historical Kharvassa activity.

Some contain enormous stone markers buried beneath their foundations.

These markers point downward.

The same inscription appears repeatedly:

*The children travel.*

*The Mother remains.*

No surviving tradition explains the phrase.

## Incident UMB-028-09

During ████, an expedition attempted to attach tracking equipment to one of Kharvassa's exposed necks.

The device remained attached for approximately seventeen minutes.

Initial readings suggested movement beneath the sand at approximately 6 km/h.

The tracker then accelerated.

**13:41** — 8 km/h

**13:43** — 19 km/h

**13:44** — 41 km/h

**13:45** — 116 km/h

**13:46** — tracker depth exceeded equipment limit.

**13:47** — signal received from Station B.

Station B was located ██████ kilometres away.

**13:48** — signal received from original location.

**13:49** — both signals active simultaneously.

████████████████████████████████████████████████

No further tracking attempts have been authorised.

## Relationship with Axius

Kharvassa exhibits no consistent vulnerability to Axius.

However, unusually high Axius concentrations have been recorded within areas recently traversed by Sandwyrms participating in a Brood Call.

Whether the creatures produce, transport or accumulate Axius remains unknown.

Direct exposure to Kharvassa has caused several anomalous effects.

These include:

- Axius techniques manifesting beneath the user rather than at the intended target;
- persistent perception of movement below solid ground;
- inability to correctly judge distance;
- temporary attraction of nearby Sandwyrms;
- and auditory hallucinations resembling movement inside walls or floors.

One surviving practitioner described the sensation as:

*Standing on something that was breathing.*

No geological movement was recorded during the incident.

## Current Status

Kharvassa is classified as:

**ACTIVE — DORMANT**

Its exact location is unknown.

This designation is controversial.

Kharvassa may not possess a single fixed location.

The last confirmed major manifestation occurred in ████.

Sandwyrm migration patterns continue to be monitored throughout Halingo.

Three unexplained Brood Call events have occurred since the last confirmed sighting.

During the most recent event, approximately ████ Sandwyrms travelled into an uninhabited section of desert.

None returned.

Satellite monitoring detected no surface manifestation.

Seismic equipment recorded:

02:11 — low-frequency movement

02:16 — movement increasing

02:23 — Sandwyrm migration reaches central zone

02:31 — surface movement ceases

02:34 — seismic event

02:35 — second seismic event

02:37 — ██████████████████

02:41 — all readings cease

The following morning the desert surface showed no visible disturbance.

**ENCOUNTER GUIDANCE // UMB-028**

Within [Halingo](/content/locations/halingo.md):

**Never follow migrating Sandwyrms.**

**Do not investigate mass Sandwyrm gatherings.**

**Do not enter areas where normal Sandwyrm territorial behaviour suddenly ceases.**

**Do not assume exposed heads represent separate organisms.**

If multiple Sandwyrm species begin travelling in the same direction:

**EVACUATE THE REGION.**

If movement is felt beneath the ground after the Sandwyrms disappear:

YOU HAVE WAITED TOO LONG.

> When the children travel together, do not ask where they are going.
> Their mother already knows.
>
> — Halingo desert proverb

name: Knelhen
summary: Coral-shelled guardian creature seen only around Armada: gentle with its people, ferocious in defence of its territory.

fields.habitat: Shipyards, floating districts and the waters around Armada

body:
**Knelhens** are very rare guardian-creatures spotted only in Armada, but they exist in the ocean world-wide. They are calm and surprisingly friendly toward the people of the floating city, but become ferociously violent in it's territory.

## Appearance

Knelhens are large, heavy-bodied creatures with powerful limbs, fin-like growths and a shell-like back covered in coral, barnacles and other sea growths.

They often appear decorated by the sea itself, as though part beast and part drifting wreck.

## Behaviour

Knelhens are intelligent, social and unusually gentle around those they recognise as part of Armada.

They may allow trusted people to approach, follow workers through the docks or sleep beneath moored vessels.

When threatened, however, a Knelhen becomes immensely dangerous. They defend themselves and others with sudden speed and overwhelming force.

## Habitat

Knelhens are found around the ocean, but only have been spotted in Armada.

## Danger

A peaceful Knelhen is approachable. An angered Knelhen is a disaster. Stories have been told of them tearing through whole boarding parties, smashing weak hulls. Conversely, rare stories tell of them defendng wounded sailors against larger prey.

## Challenge Rating

Knelhens have a **Challenge Rating of 8**.

They are dangerous because of their strength, resilience and protective instincts. Most do not attack without cause, but once provoked they are capable of killing heavily armed opponents.

## Adventure Uses

A Knelhen might:

- Guard a hidden area of Armada
- Adopt an unusual interest in a party member
- Defend a ship carrying important cargo
- Attack anyone disturbing a particular wreck
- Be mistaken for a monster when it is actually protecting someone

name: Lanthart
summary: Small, friendly deer-like creature of Nareth whose glowing tail-orb lights the herd's way through the rainforest.
body:
**Lantharts** are small deer-like creatures found only in the rainforests and wetlands of Nareth. They are recognised by the warm light carried at the end of their tails.

Lanthart are naturally friendly and often approach travellers who behave calmly. They rarely remain close to loud, violent or heavily armed groups.

## Appearance

Lantharts have light bodies, branching wooden antlers and patches of green growth resembling moss or leaves.

The orb at the end of the tail produces a soft yellow light. Its brightness increases when the creature is excited, frightened or attempting to attract the attention of another Lanthart.

## Behaviour

Lantharts live in small herds and use their tail-lights to remain together within dense vegetation.

They are curious, playful and unusually trusting. A Lanthart may follow travellers for several hours, particularly when offered fruit.

When threatened, nearby Lantharts rapidly flash their lights to warn the rest of the herd before fleeing into the undergrowth.

## Habitat

Lantharts are found near rivers, flooded forests and rainforest clearings throughout Nareth.

Their light attracts insects, which in turn draw birds and other small animals. A resting herd often becomes the centre of a small temporary ecosystem.

They do not survive well outside Nareth. Lantharts removed from the region gradually lose their light, appetite and energy.

## Relationship with People

Many Narethian communities consider Lantharts signs of safe passage.

Travellers sometimes follow their lights through dense forests, as the creatures instinctively avoid unstable ground, deep water and the territories of large predators. Locals deeply disapprove of this process.

Harming a Lanthart is considered cruel in most settlements. Capturing one for sale is forbidden by several local communities.

## Challenge Rating

Lantharts have a **Challenge Rating of 1/8**.

They are not aggressive and normally flee from combat. Their speed, small size and warning flashes make them difficult to approach unnoticed.

## Adventure Uses

A Lanthart might:

- Guide travellers through a dangerous swamp
- Lead the party towards an injured creature
- Refuse to enter an apparently safe area
- Be targeted by poachers
- Become separated from its herd
- Reveal something hidden when its tail-light grows brighter

name: Mournback
summary: Enormous, asymmetrical long-armed abomination that haunts ruins and keeps fighting through catastrophic injury.

fields.habitat: Ruins, forests, caves and abandoned settlements

body:
**Mournbacks** are enormous predatory Abominations distinguished by elongated limbs, exposed growths of bone and tendon, and extreme asymmetry between different parts of the body.

They are rare, highly territorial, and exceptionally violent once disturbed.

Despite their appearance, Mournbacks are living animals rather than [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md), and confirmed specimens have been successfully killed.

**DANGER — CR 12**

A Mournback should never be approached by an unprepared travelling party.

Its reach, speed and capacity to continue fighting after catastrophic injury make close engagement particularly dangerous.

## Appearance

Adult Mournbacks stand significantly taller than a human when fully upright.

Their anatomy varies between individuals, but common characteristics include:

- an emaciated torso;
- disproportionately long forelimbs;
- one limb frequently developing far larger than the other;
- exposed bone, tendon and hardened growths;
- thick mats of coarse hair;
- elongated claws;
- and horn-like or branch-like growth around the head and shoulders.

The oversized arm is particularly dangerous.

Mournbacks use it both for locomotion and as a striking limb capable of overturning carts, breaking doors and throwing adult humans considerable distances.

**Abomination variance**

No two Mournbacks are anatomically identical.

The species is identified by recurring skeletal and behavioural traits rather than exact appearance.

## Behaviour

Mournbacks are solitary and strongly territorial.

Most spend daylight hours concealed within ruins, caves, abandoned structures or dense woodland.

They become considerably more active at dusk and during poor weather.

Once threatened, a Mournback displays little concern for self-preservation.

Individuals have continued attacking after:

- loss of an eye;
- broken limbs;
- deep abdominal injuries;
- extensive blood loss;
- and partial severing of smaller extremities.

This behaviour has led to the mistaken belief that they cannot feel pain.

Dissection suggests otherwise.

They simply do not reliably respond to it.

## Hunting

Mournbacks are opportunistic predators.

They favour large prey and appear particularly sensitive to sudden movement and loud noise.

Their usual attack begins with a rapid charge followed by sweeping strikes from the enlarged forelimb.

At close range they bite, claw and attempt to pin prey beneath their body.

They are capable climbers despite their size, though their unusual proportions make descending considerably less graceful.

## Origin

The origin of Mournbacks remains uncertain.

Their anatomy is too inconsistent for them to represent a conventional species without significant biological abnormality.

Most scholars classify them as true **Abominations** — organisms whose development has been radically altered through mutation, environmental influence, Axius, or another poorly understood process.

Whether Mournbacks reproduce normally has never been confirmed.

Juvenile specimens are unknown.

**FIELD BIOLOGY NOTE**

Every recovered Mournback has been physically mature.

No nest has been identified.

No egg has been identified.

No pregnant specimen has been identified.

This does not mean that they appear from nowhere.

It means we do not currently know where they begin.

## Habitat

Mournbacks favour isolated locations capable of sheltering their considerable size.

Common territories include:

- abandoned settlements;
- ruined religious structures;
- forested valleys;
- cave systems;
- derelict estates;
- and old fortifications.

Their territories are usually recognisable through broken vegetation, deep claw marks and partially consumed carcasses.

## Relationship with People

Mournbacks do not ordinarily seek populated settlements.

Most attacks occur when travellers, hunters or scavengers unknowingly enter established territory.

Once a Mournback associates a settlement with food or repeated disturbance, removal becomes necessary.

Professional monster hunters occasionally accept such contracts.

Casual attempts to kill one are responsible for a disproportionate number of Mournback-related deaths.

## Combat Assessment

**Threat: Extreme**

Mournbacks combine exceptional reach, physical strength and durability with unpredictable movement.

They are particularly dangerous in confined environments where their sweeping attacks can control large areas.

Experienced hunters favour open ground, ranged attacks and repeated injury to the legs.

## Known Weaknesses

Mournbacks are difficult to kill, but not unusually resistant to conventional injury.

Effective approaches include:

- crippling the legs before closing distance;
- attacking from several directions;
- maintaining significant separation from the enlarged arm;
- exploiting their tendency to pursue the nearest moving target;
- and sustained blood loss.

Fire can frighten some individuals but should not be considered reliable.

## Axius

Mournback tissue frequently contains elevated but highly irregular concentrations of Axius.

Whether Axius causes their abnormal development or simply accumulates within already altered tissue remains disputed.

Attempts to deliberately reproduce Mournback-like mutations have not produced viable organisms.

## Adventure Uses

A Mournback may serve as:

- a dangerous creature occupying abandoned ruins;
- the cause of missing travellers;
- a monster-hunting contract;
- an Abomination whose corpse is valuable to researchers;
- evidence of contamination affecting local wildlife;
- or a creature driven from its old territory by something considerably worse.

> A dead Mournback is dangerous only in the usual ways. Make certain it is dead first.

name: Nhalyss
summary: The Unblinking Hunger: the only Umbuso rated Existential, manifesting worldwide as eyes and mouths.
body:
> **UMB-097 IS THE ONLY ENTITY CURRENTLY ASSIGNED AN EXISTENTIAL THREAT CLASSIFICATION.**
>
> Information contained within this archive has been deliberately reduced.
>
> Do not reproduce unrestricted visual records.
>
> Do not attempt to establish a complete sighting map.
>
> Do not compare eye arrangements between manifestations without authorisation.

*Sanitised reconstruction of UMB-097. Direct photographic material is not available for general archival access.*

**Nhalyss**, commonly referred to as **the Unblinking Hunger**, is an [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md) documented throughout almost every known region of the world.

Unlike other Umbuso, UMB-097 possesses no recognised territory, habitat or environmental preference.

And, on at least one confirmed occasion, █████████████████████████.

Whether these manifestations represent the movement of a single organism, multiple individuals, or portions of an entity which does not occupy space conventionally remains unresolved.

Nhalyss is considered the most dangerous Umbuso presently known.

**ARCHIVAL DIRECTIVE UMB-097**

If you have accessed this page because you believe you have personally observed UMB-097:

**STOP READING.**

Close all visual records.

Move to an enclosed location.

Do not attempt to verify the sighting.

Contact the appropriate authority using protocol ██████.

If you are currently able to see UMB-097:

DO NOT CONTINUE READING THIS DOCUMENT.

## Overview

Nhalyss is a highly irregular organism consisting of numerous looping, serpentine structures covered in eyes, jaws and pale appendages.

No central body has ever been conclusively identified.

Individual segments intersect, knot and disappear behind one another in ways which make the organism's overall anatomy impossible to reconstruct.

Most visible surfaces possess eyes.

Many also possess mouths.

Some possess both.

The creature's appearance differs substantially between observations.

This was originally attributed to movement.

It is now known that separate observers viewing the same manifestation may perceive different numbers of eyes, mouths and body segments simultaneously.

There is no verified complete description of Nhalyss.

Every witness sees less than the whole.

It is unknown whether a whole exists.

## Appearance

The most consistently reported component of Nhalyss is a series of thick golden-brown or orange structures forming loops, coils and interconnected rings.

Numerous eyes are embedded directly into these structures.

Confirmed iris colours range the whole spectrum, including colours previously unseen.

Large pale jaws emerge between the eyes.

These mouths contain irregular teeth and smaller tendril-like structures.

Individual jaws sometimes appear connected to the larger body.

Others appear suspended inside open loops with no visible supporting anatomy.

Attempts to establish a consistent count have failed.

The highest verified single-observer report contained:

████ eyes.

████ mouths.

████ distinct loops.

The photographic record from the same encounter contains fewer of all three.

## Scale

Nhalyss possesses no reliable recorded size.

Manifestations have ranged from structures small enough to appear inside a building to entities spanning significant portions of the visible horizon.

It is unknown whether Nhalyss changes size.

An alternative hypothesis proposes that observers are seeing the same organism from differing apparent distances.

This explanation creates a separate problem.

During Incident UMB-097-14, observers positioned over 300 kilometres apart simultaneously reported Nhalyss appearing approximately fifty metres away.

Both were correct according to available imaging.

**SMALLEST CONFIRMED MANIFESTATION:** 4.2 m

**LARGEST CONFIRMED MANIFESTATION:** ██████████

**MEASURABLE MASS:** None

**CONFIRMED CENTRAL BODY:** None

**NUMBER OF INDIVIDUALS:** Unknown

**ASSUMPTION OF SINGLE INDIVIDUAL:** UNSAFE

## Distribution

Nhalyss is the only currently recognised Umbuso with a confirmed global distribution.

Probable UMB-097 manifestations have occurred within or near:

- [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md);
- Skgurr;
- Shinkira;
- Nareth;
- [Halingo](/content/locations/halingo.md);
- Hjarthland;
- and numerous additional territories.

No environmental pattern has been identified.

Temperature is irrelevant.

Altitude is irrelevant.

Population density is irrelevant.

Access to water is irrelevant.

Local Axius concentration appears irrelevant.

No known geographic barrier has prevented an appearance.

For this reason, the phrase **known region** has been removed from formal UMB-097 documentation.

Nhalyss does not have a known region.

Anywhere is within its known range.

## Simultaneous Manifestations

For much of its study, researchers assumed Nhalyss travelled rapidly between locations.

This assumption is no longer considered viable.

Multiple confirmed manifestations have occurred simultaneously.

The most significant publicly acknowledged case involved five observation sites across four regions.

All five maintained visual contact with UMB-097 during an overlapping eleven-minute period.

Each manifestation appeared different.

All produced identical anomalous responses from monitoring equipment.

When Site Three attempted to physically damage the entity, manifestations at Sites One, Two, Four and Five reacted.

The manifestation at Site Three did not.

**UMB-097-22 // SYNCHRONISED EVENT**

18:04 — visual contact, Site 1

18:06 — visual contact, Site 2

18:08 — visual contact, Site 4

18:09 — visual contact, Site 3

18:11 — visual contact, Site 5

18:14 — Site 3 fires

18:14 — Site 1 movement

18:14 — Site 2 movement

18:14 — Site 4 movement

18:14 — Site 5 movement

18:14 — Site 3 no reaction

18:15 — ████████████████████████████████

18:16 — Site 3 communications lost

No explanation has been accepted.

## The Eyes

Every known Nhalyss manifestation contains numerous eyes.

They blink independently.

Some never blink.

Their purpose is unknown.

Tracking experiments indicate that different eyes can follow separate individuals simultaneously.

Closing one's own eyes does not reliably prevent the sensation of being watched.

Neither does leaving the creature's direct line of sight.

During controlled observation, personnel behind solid structures have correctly identified the moment individual UMB-097 eyes changed orientation toward them.

No mechanism for this awareness has been determined.

**UMB-097 VISUAL PROTOCOL**

Do not maintain direct visual contact.

Do not use binocular magnification.

Do not count the eyes.

Do not attempt to determine whether two eyes belong to the same head.

Do not inspect reflections.

Do not use enhanced imaging to search for additional eyes.

If an eye appears to be looking directly toward you:

**BREAK VISUAL CONTACT IMMEDIATELY.**

## The Mouths

Nhalyss possesses numerous independent jaws.

The mouths do not appear primarily adapted for feeding.

Observed behaviour includes:

- biting nearby surfaces;
- biting other parts of Nhalyss;
- biting empty space;
- remaining open for several hours;
- moving without producing sound;
- and producing sound without visible movement.

Some have spoken.

The resulting vocalisations are heavily restricted.

Unlike [Oruvath](/content/creatures/oruvath.md), Nhalyss does not appear to mimic identifiable individuals.

Instead, recordings contain speech in multiple languages, frequently overlapping.

Most statements are incoherent.

Several recur.

*I SEE THE DOOR.*

*THIS IS NOT WHERE YOU ARE.*

*THERE ARE MORE OF YOU.*

██████████████████████████████████████████████████

*OPEN.*

The final word has appeared in recordings separated by more than three centuries.

## Visual Records

Direct photographs of Nhalyss are not publicly distributed.

This policy is not solely intended to prevent panic.

Images display several anomalies.

Independent copies of the same photograph occasionally contain different numbers of eyes.

Cropping an image may reveal features which were not visible in the uncropped original.

Colour reproduction is inconsistent.

Most concerningly, several archived photographs have changed after storage.

**IMAGE ARCHIVE INCIDENT 006-V**

Original photograph logged: 17 eyes.

Day 2: 17 eyes.

Day 11: 18 eyes.

Day 43: 21 eyes.

Day 44: photograph quarantined.

Day 45: ████████████████

Day 46: physical archive destroyed.

Digital copy reports:

**22 eyes.**

The artwork displayed on this page is a manually produced reconstruction which has passed archival review.

It should not be treated as anatomically accurate.

## Recognition Events

Several manifestations appear to begin only after an observer becomes aware of something unusual.

The sequence frequently follows:

A person notices an object.

They dismiss it.

They look again.

Additional anatomical features become visible.

Others nearby then begin seeing the same entity.

This process is called a **Recognition Event**.

It remains unclear whether Nhalyss becomes visible gradually or whether perception itself changes.

The first person to see Nhalyss is rarely the first person it was visible to.

They are only the first person who realised what they were seeing.

## Incident UMB-097-31

UMB-097-31 is the primary event responsible for the entity's current threat classification.

Most details remain restricted.

A manifestation was reported outside the settlement of ████████████████.

Initial evacuation proceeded normally.

At 06:22, a second manifestation appeared along the primary evacuation route.

At 06:29, a third was reported behind the settlement.

At 06:34, aerial observers identified additional structures.

At 06:38, regional command issued complete visual blackout protocols.

At 06:43:

██████████████████████████████████████████████████████

████████████████████████████████████████████

██████████████████████████████████████████████████████

At 07:11, all manifestations disappeared.

The settlement remained physically intact.

Population prior to incident:

██████

Population recovered:

██

No bodies were located.

No evidence of conventional predation was discovered.

The event resulted in UMB-097's reclassification from **Catastrophic** to:

EXISTENTIAL

## Why Existential?

The classification does not mean Nhalyss is known to be capable of destroying the world.

It means there is presently no demonstrated mechanism which would prevent it from affecting the entire world.

No known territory limits it.

No environmental condition prevents manifestation.

No reliable defence exists.

No confirmed method of injury exists.

No evidence suggests manifestations must occur sequentially.

And there is no verified upper limit to how many can occur simultaneously.

The theoretical worst-case scenario therefore does not involve Nhalyss travelling from region to region.

It involves Nhalyss appearing in all of them.

**UMB-097 EXTINCTION MODEL**

Current model assumes simultaneous manifestations in every major population centre.

Probability: ████████

Survival projection: ████████

MODEL WITHDRAWN.

## Historical Records

Possible descriptions of Nhalyss exist throughout unrelated cultures.

This was not recognised until modern comparative archival work.

Recurring motifs include:

- circles made of eyes;
- mouths appearing in the sky;
- many-coloured watchers;
- rings which consume themselves;
- creatures described as being “everywhere behind the world”;
- and warnings against drawing certain arrangements of eyes.

No single ancient name dominates.

Possible translated titles include:

**The Watching Hunger**

**The Mouth Around Heaven**

**The Ring of Witnesses**

**That Which Sees Behind**

**The God With No Where**

and:

██████████████████████████

The last name is not reproduced in current publications.

## The Hundred Gods

Nhalyss presents a significant problem for the historical concept of the [Hundred Gods](/content/lore/umbuso.md).

Several traditions appear to treat it differently from other Umbuso.

Rather than describing one god among many, some texts imply that Nhalyss existed **outside** the traditional count.

One damaged Shinkiran record lists several entities believed to correspond to known Umbuso.

At the bottom of the text, in a different hand, is written:

*Do not count the one made of eyes.*

*It counts us.*

Whether this refers to Nhalyss is disputed.

## Relationship with Axius

Nhalyss does not consistently suppress Axius.

Instead, Axius phenomena become increasingly difficult to localise during manifestations.

Users have reported:

- effects occurring from the wrong direction;
- abilities manifesting behind the caster;
- sensing several identical targets;
- seeing through perspectives which are not their own;
- temporary inability to distinguish nearby minds;
- and awareness of locations they have never visited.

During UMB-097-18, one practitioner correctly described a room located on another continent.

UMB-097 was simultaneously present outside both locations.

The practitioner had never travelled there.

When asked how they knew what the room looked like, they replied:

*I used the wrong eye.*

The practitioner permanently lost vision approximately three hours later.

No physical damage to either eye was identified.

## Attempts at Destruction

No attack against Nhalyss has produced a confirmed injury.

Conventional weapons may damage visible tissue.

The effect is temporary.

Destroyed eyes have reappeared.

Severed segments have disappeared.

Burned tissue has been observed intact in separate manifestations.

Attempts involving Axius have produced inconsistent outcomes.

One operation apparently destroyed an entire manifestation.

Seven minutes later, another appeared approximately ██████ kilometres away.

It contained an additional mouth.

The operation was not repeated.

## Current Status

Nhalyss is classified:

**ACTIVE — GLOBAL**

This is the only Umbuso archive in which **Active** does not indicate a confirmed current location.

It indicates that manifestations continue to occur.

No reliable method exists for predicting them.

The most recent confirmed sighting occurred on ████████.

The most recent probable sighting occurred:

████ HOURS AGO

This value is automatically removed from archived copies.

**CURRENT UMB-097 WATCH STATUS**

Known active manifestations: ██

Probable manifestations: ███

Unresolved visual anomalies: ████████

Regions unaffected historically:

**NONE**

**ENCOUNTER GUIDANCE // UMB-097**

If a suspected manifestation of Nhalyss is observed:

**DO NOT BREAK LINE OF SIGHT.**

**DO NOT PHOTOGRAPH IT.**

**DO NOT ATTEMPT TO DETERMINE WHETHER IT HAS SEEN YOU.**

If you believe you have observed it. Contact the Ambit immediately.

STOP MOVING.

CLOSE YOUR EYES.

WAIT FOR INSTRUCTIONS.

> Do not ask where it lives.
> That question assumes there is somewhere it does not.
>
> — UMB-097 Research Director ████████

name: Oruvath
summary: The Buried Choir: an Umbuso found only among extremely old ruins, whose many mouths mimic human voices.
body:
*Composite reconstruction of UMB-041 based upon surviving descriptions. Location unknown. Structures depicted are based upon Site UMB-041-C.*

**Oruvath**, commonly referred to as **the Buried Choir**, is an [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md) documented in archaeological and historical records across several otherwise unrelated regions.

Unlike most known Umbuso, Oruvath displays no confirmed geographical territory.

Every credible appearance has instead occurred among extremely old ruins.

In several cases, no evidence has been found that those ruins were ever inhabited.

The entity is characterised by a massive central body, numerous independently moving jaws, several differently coloured eyes and long structures which disappear beneath the surrounding ground.

The full organism has never been observed.

**ARCHIVAL DIRECTIVE UMB-041-A**

Personnel entering a suspected UMB-041 site are prohibited from speaking unless necessary.

If vocal communication is required, use preassigned numeric codes.

If an unidentified voice addresses personnel by name:

**DO NOT RESPOND.**

## Overview

Oruvath is one of the few Umbuso documented beyond a single cultural or geographic region.

Records consistent with UMB-041 have been recovered from:

- ruined settlements;
- abandoned religious complexes;
- subterranean chambers;
- ancient fortifications;
- isolated stone monuments;
- and archaeological sites with no known builders.

Descriptions separated by centuries repeatedly mention the same characteristics:

numerous mouths;

dark fibrous or fur-like tissue;

isolated coloured eyes;

root-like appendages;

and voices.

For much of modern scholarship, these similarities were considered coincidental.

That interpretation changed after the discovery of ████████████████.

██████████████████████████████████████████████████████

UMB-041 classification was formally established shortly afterwards.

## Appearance

Oruvath possesses a massive, irregular body covered in dark brown and black material resembling coarse fur, bark or bundled fibres.

No consistent skeletal structure has been identified.

Numerous serpentine structures emerge from the central mass.

Many terminate in jaws.

Others appear to terminate in nothing at all.

The number of visible mouths varies dramatically between reports.

The lowest confirmed count is four.

The highest is ██.

Each mouth contains several rows of pale teeth.

Their shape differs between jaws.

Some resemble the teeth of carnivorous mammals.

Others do not correspond to any known organism.

Several independent eyes are embedded throughout the visible body.

Confirmed colours include:

- yellow;
- blue;
- red;
- white;
- and ██████.

There is no evidence that the eyes correspond anatomically with individual mouths.

## The Mouths

The mouths of Oruvath are capable of speech.

This behaviour is considered the defining characteristic of UMB-041.

Different mouths appear to possess different voices.

Documented examples include:

- adult men;
- adult women;
- children;
- elderly individuals;
- unfamiliar animal-like vocalisations;
- speakers of extinct languages;
- and individuals personally known to observers.

The mouths do not ordinarily speak together.

Each appears to maintain its own vocabulary and cadence.

No confirmed voice has ever originated from a person known to still be alive.

Whether Oruvath imitates the dead, records voices it has previously encountered or possesses some other mechanism remains unknown.

## Voice Identification

The most disturbing evidence surrounding UMB-041 originates from Voice Record 17.

During investigation of Site UMB-041-B, audio equipment recorded an unidentified female voice speaking from within the ruins.

The language was not recognised by the expedition.

The recording remained unclassified for twenty-three years.

A later archaeological team identified the language as a dialect which disappeared approximately six centuries before the recording was made.

The speaker described:

*The stones are warm.*

*It has opened another mouth.*

*We should not have answered.*

A written text containing nearly identical phrasing was subsequently discovered at another archaeological site approximately ████ kilometres away.

The inscription predates the audio recording by approximately 611 years.

## Mimicry

Oruvath appears capable of reproducing voices with extraordinary accuracy.

During Incident UMB-041-04, an expedition member reported hearing another researcher call for assistance from beyond the excavation perimeter.

The researcher whose voice had been heard was standing beside them at the time.

Shortly afterwards, the voice repeated the request.

It then began addressing individual members of the expedition by name.

23:11 — voice detected east of camp.

23:13 — identity resembles Researcher Lorne.

23:13 — Lorne confirms he did not speak.

23:14 — second voice detected.

23:16 — voice uses Researcher Ishar's name.

23:17 — third voice.

23:18 — ████████████████████

23:20 — all personnel ordered silent.

23:41 — voices continue.

02:04 — voices cease.

Oruvath was not visually observed during the incident.

The excavation was abandoned the following morning.

## The Ruins

Every confirmed Oruvath manifestation is associated with ancient architecture.

Initially, researchers assumed these locations represented abandoned settlements.

Several do.

Others present a more difficult problem.

At Site UMB-041-C, investigators uncovered extensive stone structures resembling:

- towers;
- roads;
- defensive walls;
- arches;
- monuments;
- and foundations.

No domestic objects were recovered.

No tools.

No pottery.

No graves.

No food remains.

No written records.

No evidence of habitation whatsoever.

There was a city.

There is no evidence that anyone ever lived there.

Subsequent excavations discovered that several apparently architectural structures extended far deeper underground than expected.

Analysis of recovered material produced inconsistent results.

Some samples were stone.

Some were mineralised organic tissue.

Some could not be classified.

Excavation was suspended.

## Structural Association

A minority of researchers have proposed that Oruvath does not inhabit ruins.

The theory proposes that the ruins are **part of Oruvath**.

Evidence remains inconclusive.

Several structures associated with UMB-041 contain formations displaying unusual similarities to biological growth.

Examples include:

- arches containing structures resembling ribs;
- towers with repeating internal cavities;
- walls displaying branching patterns similar to blood vessels;
- stone pillars which respond weakly to heat;
- and foundations containing material genetically related to no known organism.

The theory remains officially unaccepted.

**INTERNAL NOTE**

Please stop calling Site C a city.

We do not know that.

We have never known that.

████████████████████████████████████████████

## Movement

Oruvath has rarely been observed moving its central body.

Individual heads, jaws and tendrils move extensively.

The larger organism appears largely stationary.

This may be misleading.

Historical records place apparently identical manifestations in locations separated by enormous distances.

There are three accepted possibilities:

1.  multiple Oruvath-class entities exist;
2.  Oruvath is capable of travelling between sites by an unknown method;
3.  all known sites connect to the same organism.

The third possibility is considered improbable.

It has not been eliminated.

## Subterranean Extent

Attempts to map Oruvath beneath the surface have produced contradictory results.

Ground-penetrating equipment frequently identifies large organic structures extending away from manifestation sites.

The detected structures resemble roots, veins or tunnels.

At Site UMB-041-A, one such formation was tracked for approximately 19 kilometres.

At Site UMB-041-D, a matching structure was detected.

The two sites are separated by ████████.

**VISIBLE BODY LENGTH:** Unknown

**MAXIMUM CONFIRMED SUBTERRANEAN EXTENT:** 19 km

**POSSIBLE EXTENT:** ████████████

**NUMBER OF CONFIRMED MANIFESTATION SITES:** ██

**NUMBER OF CONFIRMED INDIVIDUALS:** Unknown

No attempt has been made to physically follow these structures.

Following Incident UMB-041-08, such excavation is prohibited.

## Feeding

Oruvath has been observed consuming animals.

Its individual mouths are fully capable of tearing and ingesting conventional organic material.

It is unclear whether feeding serves a nutritional purpose.

No digestive system has been identified.

Food entering one mouth has never been observed exiting elsewhere.

The creature has also been reported biting:

- stone;
- timber;
- metal;
- masonry;
- other portions of its own body;
- and empty air.

One manifestation spent approximately six hours repeatedly biting the side of an ancient tower.

The structure displayed no visible damage.

When investigators returned after the entity disappeared, the entire interior of the tower was missing.

The exterior remained intact.

## Incident UMB-041-08

Incident UMB-041-08 resulted in the permanent prohibition of deep excavation at known sites.

A team investigating organic material beneath Site UMB-041-A opened a chamber approximately 74 metres below ground.

The chamber contained no visible manifestation.

Audio equipment recorded breathing.

The team continued.

At 14:22, drilling equipment penetrated an unidentified soft material.

At 14:23, every known mouth of the surface manifestation opened simultaneously.

No sound was produced.

At 14:24, voices were heard throughout the excavation.

██████████████████████████████████████████████████████

████████████████████████████████████████

At 14:31, surface observers reported that UMB-041 had developed three additional mouths.

The underground team contained three personnel.

Recovery operations were not authorised.

## Missing Persons

Numerous disappearances have been associated with suspected UMB-041 locations.

Physical remains are rarely recovered.

Several months or years later, expedition personnel have occasionally reported hearing voices resembling missing individuals.

This correlation cannot be conclusively verified.

One recording remains particularly controversial.

A researcher disappeared during Exploration UMB-041-02.

Eleven years later, their voice was apparently recorded from one of Oruvath's mouths.

The recording contained one sentence:

*It isn't eating us.*

████████████████████████████████████████

The remainder of the recording has never been publicly released.

## Historical Records

Possible Oruvath references appear across numerous cultures.

This is unusual for an Umbuso.

Recurring titles include translations approximating:

- The Buried Choir;
- The House of Mouths;
- The Speaking Ruin;
- The King Beneath Stones;
- The Many Hungry;
- and The City That Answers.

There is no clear evidence these traditions influenced one another.

Several originated in cultures with no known historical contact.

One recurring instruction appears in some form in nearly every surviving tradition:

**Do not answer.**

## Relationship with Axius

Oruvath produces unusual effects upon Axius related to memory and communication.

Reported phenomena include:

- hearing voices with no physical source;
- remembering conversations which never occurred;
- recognising languages the observer does not understand;
- confusing spoken thoughts with internal thoughts;
- repeating words involuntarily;
- and briefly perceiving nearby stone structures as living tissue.

Several Axius-sensitive researchers describe UMB-041 sites as extraordinarily crowded.

When asked to clarify, responses are remarkably similar.

*There are too many people talking.*

No additional individuals are physically present during these reports.

## Current Status

Oruvath is classified:

**ACTIVE — LOCATION UNKNOWN**

This classification is misleading.

Multiple probable manifestation sites are known.

What remains unknown is which, if any, currently contain the entity.

Several abandoned sites remain under passive monitoring.

No deliberate search for UMB-041 is authorised.

The most recent confirmed manifestation occurred at ████████████.

Visual contact lasted approximately nine minutes.

Audio recording continued for nearly six hours after the creature disappeared.

**FINAL AUDIO EXCERPT**

05:13 — unidentified voice

05:14 — second unidentified voice

05:17 — seven voices overlapping

05:21 — language unrecognised

05:33 — crying

05:34 — ██████████████████

05:35 — recording operator leaves station

05:37 — voice matching recording operator detected

05:38 — operator confirmed alive outside facility
