05:41 — recording terminated remotely

**ENCOUNTER GUIDANCE // UMB-041**

At suspected Oruvath sites:

**Remain silent whenever possible.**

**Do not respond to voices originating from ruins.**

**Do not investigate voices belonging to missing personnel.**

**Do not assume a familiar voice belongs to a familiar person.**

**Do not enter structures from which breathing can be heard.**

If one of the mouths speaks using **your own voice**:

LEAVE IMMEDIATELY.

DO NOT ANSWER IT.

> When the ruins call your name, remember that ruins have no mouths.
>
> — Origin unknown

name: Ritual Husk
summary: Half-formed arcane horror left behind by an interrupted or miscast ritual; only completing the ritual truly destroys it.

fields.habitat: Ruins, ritual sites, battlefields and places of magical collapse

body:
**Ritual Husks** are very rare arcane horrors formed when a ritual is interrupted, abandoned or catastrophically miscast.

They are not a species in the ordinary sense. Each Ritual Husk is the remains of a magical working that never finished becoming what it was meant to be. A miscast ritual is like a stench to them, drawn to it

## Appearance

A Ritual Husk appears as a half-formed creature of smoke, exposed magical structure and unstable flesh. Parts of its body seem complete, while others trail away into drifting vapour or collapse into empty gaps.

Its form often looks as though it is still trying to become something else.

## Origin

A ritual miscast, a broken seal, an interrupted resurrection. Powerful magical rituals

## Behaviour

A Ritual Husk behaves like a purpose that has outlived its instructions.

Some wander aimlessly. Others remain bound to the site of their creation. Many attack creatures nearby, especially spellcasters, as though trying to complete themselves through stolen magic or life.

## Danger

Ritual Husks are dangerous not only because they are physically lethal, but because they disrupt magic around them.

Their presence may cause:

- Spells to misfire
- Wards to weaken
- Ritual circles to reactivate
- Hallucinations
- Sudden bursts of arcane energy
- Magical items to behave unpredictably

A Ritual Husk should never be treated as a normal beast or monster. Destroying one often requires understanding the ritual that created it. There is only one way to 'kill' a ritual husk - by completing the failed ritual. Otherwise, one can displace it, or make it not worth their time.

## Habitat and Range

Ritual Husks can appear anywhere in Kurovia where significant magic has gone wrong.

Because they are created rather than bred, they are considered a worldwide phenomenon rather than a regional creature.

## Challenge Rating

Ritual Husks have a **Challenge Rating of 9**.

They are powerful, unpredictable and especially dangerous to parties relying heavily on magic.

## Adventure Uses

A Ritual Husk might:

- Haunt the site of a failed ritual
- Be the true cause of a noble family's curse
- Hunt a bloodline linked to its creation
- Guard a place no longer remembers why it was sealed
- Be mistaken for a demon, ghost or summoned creature

name: Saqramallki
summary: The Hanging Orchard: a Narethian Umbuso that passes for a rotted tree hung with corpse-like pods.
body:
> **DO NOT APPROACH TREE-LIKE MASS GROWTHS IN THE NARETH INTERIOR.**
>
> UMB-034 may remain motionless for extended periods and is frequently mistaken for a dead tree or ruined growth.
>
> Suspended bodies, pods or fruit-like sacs should be treated as confirmation of active territory.

*Sanitised reconstruction of UMB-034 within flooded Nareth jungle ruins.*

**Saqramallki** (pronounced **SAH-krah-MAHL-kee**) is an [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md) exclusive to Nareth.

It resembles a colossal rotted tree with root-limbs, a warped humanoid trunk, and branches from which corpse-like pods hang in clusters.

Although often mistaken for part of the forest, it is animate, territorial, and highly dangerous when disturbed.

## Overview

Saqramallki inhabits deep rainforest, swamp, and drowned ruins far from major settlements.

It remains still for long periods, blending into the surrounding jungle, then moves suddenly when its territory is entered.

Saqramallki is not a tree.

It is a predator that survives by being mistaken for one.

## Behaviour

UMB-034 appears to respond to intrusion, noise, fire, and cutting activity.

When active, it uses root-like limbs to drag itself forward and seize nearby organisms.

Victims are believed to be hung from its branches or partially incorporated into the swollen masses around its body.

Whether the suspended forms are food, trophies, or growth structures remains unknown.

**FIELD NOTE**

The branches were already full before the expedition arrived.

At least some of them were old.

Two were still speaking.

## Territory

Saqramallki is known only from Nareth.

Confirmed sites are marked by:

- black standing water;
- heavy root spread over old stone;
- unusual silence among animals;
- and suspended remains high in the canopy.

These signs make it more avoidable than some Umbuso, though few survive long enough to recognise the pattern twice.

## Current Status

UMB-034 is classified:

**ACTIVE — NARETH INTERIOR**

Its precise location is unknown.

This should not be interpreted as absence.

It indicates only that no expedition is currently maintaining visual contact.

**ENCOUNTER GUIDANCE // UMB-034**

**DO NOT SHELTER BENEATH IT.**

**DO NOT CUT HANGING PODS OR BODIES FREE.**

**DO NOT USE FIRE TO TEST WHETHER IT IS ALIVE.**

Withdraw immediately if multiple corpse-like growths are visible from a single canopy structure.

If roots begin moving under shallow water:

RETREAT WITHOUT ATTEMPTING RECOVERY.

> In Nareth, even the dead trees wait for you to come closer.
>
> — Recovery note appended to Incident UMB-034-07

name: Shellbill
summary: Docile, duck-billed, shelled semi-aquatic creature common across the waterways of Ordon, Skgurr, Shinkira and Nareth.
body:
The **Shellbill** is a widespread semi-aquatic creature found throughout [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md), Skgurr, Shinkira and Nareth.

Recognisable by its duck-like head, broad paddling feet and heavy protective shell, the Shellbill is one of the most familiar freshwater animals across these regions.

They are generally harmless, social and curious creatures, although adults become remarkably stubborn when threatened.

## Appearance

Shellbills possess a body plan combining characteristics usually associated with waterfowl and shelled reptiles.

An adult typically possesses:

- a short, broad bill;
- smooth orange, yellow or brown plumage around the head and limbs;
- four powerful paddle-like feet;
- a large dark green or olive shell;
- and a prominent feathered tail extending beyond the rear of the shell.

The shell grows throughout the animal's life.

Young Shellbills possess relatively soft, brightly coloured shells which gradually darken and harden as they mature.

Older individuals may develop scratches, chips, algae and mineral staining across the shell.

**Identification note:**

Despite their appearance, Shellbills cannot fully withdraw into their shells.

They can, however, pull the head and limbs close enough to the body that the shell protects most vulnerable areas.

## Behaviour

Shellbills spend much of their lives in or around shallow water.

They are most commonly observed:

- paddling slowly across ponds and rivers;
- searching mud for food;
- resting together along banks;
- sleeping partially submerged;
- or following other Shellbills in loose family groups.

They are highly social.

Groups of between three and twelve individuals are common, although considerably larger gatherings may occur in areas with plentiful food.

Young Shellbills remain close to adults for several months after hatching.

Adults have been observed physically placing themselves between juveniles and perceived threats.

Despite their generally placid temperament, Shellbills can become extremely difficult to move once frightened.

A threatened individual usually lowers itself against the ground, pulls its limbs beneath the shell and simply refuses to move.

This behaviour has frustrated farmers, travellers and railway workers for generations.

## Diet

Shellbills are omnivorous.

Their diet consists primarily of:

- aquatic vegetation;
- seeds;
- grasses;
- insects;
- freshwater snails;
- small crustaceans;
- worms;
- fallen fruit;
- and occasional small fish.

They spend considerable periods with their bills beneath the surface, filtering soft sediment for edible material.

Shellbills living near human settlements quickly learn to associate people with food.

Feeding wild Shellbills is discouraged in several large cities because habituated animals have a tendency to occupy roads, docks and public gardens in large numbers.

## Shell

The shell is composed of overlapping hardened plates.

Colour varies between populations, but dark olive green is by far the most common.

Unlike ordinary protective shells, a Shellbill's carapace contains a thin layer of soft tissue beneath each plate.

Damaged plates can therefore slowly regrow.

This process may take several years.

The shell is highly resistant to biting predators and offers effective protection against falling debris and smaller projectiles.

It also makes the animal surprisingly heavy.

An adult Shellbill may appear small enough to lift until someone actually attempts to do so.

“Never pick up a Shellbill unless you're prepared to discover how much a pond weighs.”

— Ordon saying

## Swimming

Shellbills are considerably more agile in water than their appearance suggests.

Their broad feet provide powerful propulsion, while the shell naturally stabilises the body.

At normal speed they move slowly and smoothly.

When frightened, however, a Shellbill can produce a sudden burst of speed which frequently surprises observers.

They are capable of remaining underwater for several minutes.

Rather than actively swimming at depth, Shellbills commonly walk along riverbeds while searching for food.

Their shell provides enough weight to prevent them from floating uncontrollably toward the surface.

## Reproduction

Shellbills lay small clutches of thick-shelled eggs in nests dug into soft earth near water.

Both parents may remain near the nest.

After hatching, juvenile Shellbills instinctively seek water.

Their shells are initially flexible and require several months to fully harden.

Young Shellbills possess brighter yellow-orange plumage than most adults.

This colouration becomes progressively darker with age.

Family groups are particularly protective during this period.

## Distribution

Shellbills possess an unusually broad natural range.

Populations are established throughout:

- [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md);
- Skgurr;
- Shinkira;
- and Nareth.

They favour rivers, lakes, marshes, canals, flooded farmland and sheltered coastal wetlands.

Their adaptability has allowed them to thrive in both wilderness and heavily populated environments.

Regional populations differ slightly in size, shell colour and behaviour.

## Ordon

Shellbills are a common sight around the canals, waterways and industrial reservoirs of [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md).

Urban populations have adapted exceptionally well to human activity.

They can frequently be found beneath bridges, beside locks and around public waterways.

Ordon Shellbills tend to possess particularly dark shells, likely due to generations of staining from soot and industrial sediment.

Workers traditionally regard a Shellbill sleeping near a factory entrance as good luck.

A Shellbill sitting directly **in** the entrance is regarded less favourably.

## Skgurr

Skgurr contains some of the largest known Shellbills.

Coastal populations inhabit sheltered inlets, estuaries and freshwater pools close to the sea.

Their shells are often thicker than those of inland populations.

During severe storms, Skgurr Shellbills gather in large groups behind rocks or within protected coastal pools.

They appear capable of detecting worsening weather several hours before conditions become visibly dangerous.

For this reason, some fishing communities historically watched local Shellbill behaviour when deciding whether to leave harbour.

## Shinkira

Shellbills are particularly common throughout the agricultural regions of Shinkira.

They inhabit rice fields, irrigation channels, temple ponds and slow-moving rivers.

Unlike populations elsewhere, Shinkiran Shellbills are often tolerated directly within farmland because their feeding removes many insects and freshwater pests.

Several rural communities keep semi-domesticated populations.

These animals are not usually confined.

They simply learn where food is available and repeatedly return.

Small decorative sculptures of Shellbills are also common around ponds and gardens.

## Nareth

In Nareth, Shellbills are most strongly associated with wetlands and broad river systems.

Local populations commonly travel considerable distances between seasonal feeding grounds.

Large migrations may involve hundreds of individuals moving downstream together.

Nareth Shellbills are usually somewhat lighter in colour than their counterparts elsewhere.

Whether this represents a distinct subspecies remains disputed.

## Relationship with Humans

Shellbills adapt remarkably well to human settlement.

They display little natural fear of people in areas where they are not hunted.

Some individuals become sufficiently accustomed to particular households or businesses that they return to the same location for years.

Domestication has occurred independently in several regions.

Domestic Shellbills are primarily kept as:

- garden animals;
- pest control;
- ornamental pond animals;
- companions;
- and occasionally sources of eggs.

They are rarely kept for meat.

Historically this was partly practical: killing an animal protected by a heavy shell requires considerably more effort than keeping conventional livestock.

Modern attitudes are generally more sentimental.

Shellbills have developed a reputation as peaceful, slightly foolish animals.

This reputation is not entirely deserved.

They possess excellent long-term spatial memory and can remember feeding locations for years.

## Temperament

Wild Shellbills are normally docile.

They may approach humans out of curiosity, particularly in areas where feeding is common.

Aggression is usually limited to:

- guarding nests;
- protecting juveniles;
- competition over food;
- or responding to attempts to physically move them.

A defensive Shellbill may hiss, snap its bill or strike with its forelimbs.

Their bite is painful but rarely dangerous.

The greatest risk generally comes from attempting to lift a frightened adult and dropping it.

## Predators

Young Shellbills are vulnerable to numerous predators.

Adults have considerably fewer natural enemies.

The combination of thick shell, aquatic mobility and group behaviour makes them difficult prey.

Large predators may still attack them, particularly by targeting the head or limbs.

When threatened as a group, Shellbills frequently cluster together with juveniles in the centre.

Individuals around the outside face outward.

The resulting formation has been compared to a pile of armoured ducks.

## Axius

Shellbills demonstrate no particularly unusual relationship with Axius.

However, their shells absorb trace minerals from the surrounding environment throughout their lives.

In regions with naturally high Axius concentrations, old Shellbill shells may therefore display extremely weak Axius retention.

This effect is harmless.

Claims that carrying a discarded Shellbill plate provides protection from supernatural creatures are considered folklore.

This has not prevented such plates from being sold as charms.

## Regional Names

Due to their broad distribution, Shellbills possess numerous local names.

| Region       | Common Names         |
|--------------|----------------------|
| [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md)    | Shellbill, Canalback |
| Skgurr   | Stormshell, Baybill  |
| Shinkira | Shellbill, Pondback  |
| Nareth   | Riverback, Shellbill |

**Shellbill** has become the most widely used scholarly and international term.

## Notes

Shellbills are sometimes incorrectly described as hybrids.

There is no evidence that they originated through crossbreeding between existing animals.

Their combination of avian and reptilian characteristics represents their normal anatomy.

Fossil evidence suggests creatures recognisably similar to modern Shellbills have existed for a considerable period of time.

They are therefore considered a naturally occurring lineage rather than an artificially created species.

name: Sunsnare
summary: Burrowing Halingan ambush predator that lures prey with a false desert flower and drags it beneath the sand.

fields.habitat: Deserts, dry scrubland and dune edges

body:
**Sunsnares** are burrowing predators native to [Halingo](/content/locations/halingo.md). They disguise themselves as desert flowers, remaining motionless until prey comes close enough to seize.

When a target approaches, the Sunsnare erupts from beneath the sand, drags the victim down and feeds below the surface.

## Appearance

A Sunsnare has a low, muscular body, powerful digging claws and a lure resembling a pale desert flower. When buried, only this false bloom remains visible above the sand.

## Behaviour

Sunsnares are patient ambush hunters. They bury themselves beneath loose ground and wait for animals, travellers or scavengers to approach the lure.

They attack suddenly, using their weight and claws to pull prey off balance and beneath the sand.

## Hunting

The false flower is used as bait. Some creatures approach out of curiosity, while desperate travellers may mistake it for a real sign of water or plant life.

Experienced desert guides warn against any bloom found growing alone in open sand.

## Challenge Rating

Sunsnares have a **Challenge Rating of 2**.

They are dangerous because of their ambush tactics rather than speed or endurance. A prepared traveller can avoid them, but the unwary may be killed before they understand the threat.

name: Tathis
summary: The Following Sign: an Umbuso that manifests through a rune; whoever recognises it is stalked and killed.
body:
> **DO NOT REPRODUCE THE TRIGGERING RUNE OUTSIDE AUTHORISED MATERIAL.**
>
> UMB-076 is associated with a visual cognitohazard.
>
> Confirmed exposure occurs upon recognising the rune.
>
> Post-exposure subjects report persistent stalking phenomena followed by fatal attack.

**Tathis**, commonly called **the Following Sign**, is an [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md) believed to manifest through a specific rune.

Individuals who view the rune become marked.

Following exposure, the subject is stalked by UMB-076 over a variable period before being killed.

The creature itself is rarely observed clearly.

Most records describe only partial glimpses, silhouettes, movement in peripheral vision, or signs of approach shortly before the attack.

## Overview

UMB-076 is unusual among the Umbuso in that its primary danger does not arise from territorial presence, direct predation, or large-scale destruction.

Instead, the hazard is initiated by **visual recognition** of a specific rune.

Once the rune is seen and consciously processed, the subject is considered exposed.

The rune is not a symbol of UMB-076.

The rune **is** the encounter.

Available evidence suggests that Tathis does not attack immediately.

It follows.

It waits.

Then it kills.

## The Rune

The triggering image is treated as restricted visual material.

Surviving descriptions characterise it as an irregular pale mark with soft edges and an asymmetrical outline.

Minor variations in reproduction appear possible without preventing activation.

Because of this, exact duplication is not considered necessary for the hazard to persist.

**ARCHIVAL NOTE**

Do not assume that an altered copy is safe.

Do not circulate traced versions.

Do not test partial reproductions without approval.

## Post-Exposure Progression

Known cases follow a broadly similar pattern:

- initial exposure to the rune;
- a symptom-free interval;
- recurring sensations of being watched;
- sightings of a distant, malformed figure or movement;
- progressive increase in proximity;
- fatal physical encounter.

The duration of the stalking period varies considerably.

Some subjects survive for days.

Others survive for several weeks.

No confirmed subject has permanently escaped once exposure has occurred.

## Manifestation

Descriptions of Tathis are inconsistent, but several recurring traits appear in surviving testimony:

- an unnaturally thin or misshapen humanoid outline;
- jerking or unnatural movement;
- damp, distorted or broken-limbed motion;
- silence during visual approach;
- and sudden extreme violence at close range.

Most victims die before providing a full description.

*I only ever saw it properly once.*

*It was already close enough to touch me.*

██████████████████████████████████████████

## Lethality

Tathis typically kills exposed subjects through direct physical attack.

Recovered bodies demonstrate severe trauma.

The exact method varies.

This has led some scholars to argue that the entity's form may shift between encounters, or that only portions of the attack are consistently perceptible.

UMB-076 is rated **L2** not because every encounter is instantaneously fatal, but because successful survival following a full stalking cycle is extremely rare.

## Containment

Despite its frightening reputation, Tathis receives a comparatively high containment score.

The reason is straightforward:

Avoiding the rune prevents the encounter.

Controlling the rune limits the threat.

Archive policy therefore focuses on:

- suppressing unauthorised copies;
- restricting visual circulation;
- isolating contaminated documents;
- and monitoring suspected exposure events.

No confirmed method exists for saving an already marked individual.

Containment applies primarily to **information control**, not neutralisation of the entity itself.

## Distribution

UMB-076 has no fixed territory.

Cases have been recorded in multiple unrelated regions.

However, every confirmed encounter begins with prior rune exposure.

For this reason, Tathis is not considered a roaming regional Umbuso in the same sense as [Vaelkr](/content/creatures/vaelkr.md) or [Nhalyss](/content/creatures/nhalyss.md).

Its range is defined by the movement of the symbol.

## Knowledge

UMB-076 is comparatively well documented by Umbuso standards.

Its activation condition is clear.

Its general progression is clear.

Its likely outcome is clear.

What remains unknown is the true nature of the entity itself:

- whether Tathis physically travels;
- whether it manifests near the victim;
- whether the rune summons it;
- or whether the rune simply allows it to perceive the observer.

## Current Status

UMB-076 is classified:

**ACTIVE — INFORMATION-ASSOCIATED**

No permanent physical habitat is known.

The triggering rune remains in restricted archival storage.

Additional copies are presumed to exist outside official control.

**ENCOUNTER GUIDANCE // UMB-076**

If exposure to the rune is suspected:

**DO NOT RECIRCULATE THE IMAGE.**

**DO NOT ATTEMPT TO WARN OTHERS BY SHOWING IT TO THEM.**

**DO NOT CREATE NEW COPIES FROM MEMORY.**

Isolate the exposed subject.

Begin continuous observation.

Any report of a distant recurring figure should be treated as confirmation of active stalking.

> The safest way to survive Tathis is never to know what it looks like.
>
> — UMB-076 handling memorandum

name: Ulveth
summary: The Invitation: an Umbuso known only through a mark that draws harmful people, creatures and events to the object bearing it.
body:
> **DO NOT REPRODUCE THE UMB-033 MARK ON PHYSICAL OBJECTS.**
>
> The effect does not require deliberate activation.
>
> Objects bearing a sufficiently accurate representation must be treated as active hazard sources.

*UMB-033 triggering mark withheld. This archive does not contain a reproduction.*

**Ulveth**, commonly called **the Invitation**, is an [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md) known exclusively through a rune-like marking associated with an anomalous phenomenon termed **Malign Convergence**.

When the mark is inscribed upon an object, harmful people, creatures and circumstances become increasingly likely to converge upon it.

The marked object itself undergoes no known physical change.

Everything around it does.

## Overview

The UMB-033 mark can be applied to almost any physical object.

Documented examples include:

- jewellery;
- weapons;
- doors;
- vehicles;
- buildings;
- clothing;
- books;
- currency;
- and living organisms.

Once activated, adverse events begin occurring around the marked target at rates substantially exceeding chance.

UMB-033 does not make the marked object dangerous.

It makes dangerous things find it.

## Malign Convergence

Researchers avoid the traditional description that the mark **“draws evil.”**

The phrase is scientifically imprecise.

It is also remarkably difficult to replace.

Known convergence events include:

- predators approaching normally avoided settlements;
- hostile creatures changing established migration routes;
- violent individuals becoming interested in marked possessions;
- thefts;
- fires;
- equipment failures;
- structural accidents;
- disease outbreaks;
- unusually severe weather;
- and chains of statistically improbable misfortune.

No common physical mechanism links these events.

**UMB-033 RESEARCH NOTE**

The rune does not appear to attract a particular substance, organism or energy.

It attracts **outcomes**.

This wording is provisional.

It is also deeply unsatisfactory.

## Escalation

The effect typically begins subtly.

Early incidents are easily dismissed as coincidence.

A marked traveller loses supplies.

A hostile animal approaches camp.

A wheel breaks.

A stranger attempts a robbery.

If the mark remains in place, incidents generally increase in both frequency and severity.

**OBSERVED PROGRESSION**

I — coincidence

II — recurring misfortune

III — hostile convergence

IV — serious casualty risk

V — ██████████████████

Stage V has been removed from general field documentation.

## Selection

UMB-033 appears capable of producing circumstances appropriate to its environment.

A marked ship does not attract the same hazards as a marked house.

A marked person does not experience the same events as a marked weapon.

This has produced significant disagreement regarding whether Ulveth:

- predicts dangerous possibilities;
- influences probability;
- attracts existing hostile agents;
- creates new hostile circumstances;
- or possesses some form of intelligence.

There is currently insufficient evidence to distinguish between these models.

## Human Behaviour

One of the most troubling aspects of UMB-033 involves human subjects.

Individuals with no previous connection to a marked object may become unusually interested in it.

This interest can manifest as:

- curiosity;
- envy;
- theft;
- fixation;
- anger;
- or deliberate violence.

Affected individuals do not report external control.

They generally provide plausible reasons for their actions.

SUBJECT: Why did you enter the property?

DETAINEE: I wanted what was inside.

SUBJECT: You did not know what was inside.

DETAINEE: I know.

SUBJECT: Then why?

DETAINEE: It felt like there should be something worth taking.

Whether this constitutes mental influence or probability manipulation is unknown.

## Incident UMB-033-12

A reproduction of the mark was unknowingly engraved upon a freight container.

The container remained in transit for nine days.

During that period:

**Day 1** — shipping documentation misplaced.

**Day 2** — attempted theft.

**Day 4** — transport vehicle mechanical failure.

**Day 5** — second theft attempt.

**Day 6** — unidentified predator entered storage facility.

**Day 7** — warehouse fire.

**Day 8** — ██████████████████████

**Day 9** — marking identified and destroyed.

No further abnormal incidents were reported.

The contents of the container were ordinary ceramics.

## Containment

UMB-033 is unusually manageable for an Umbuso.

The mark requires a physical representation.

Removing or destroying that representation usually terminates further convergence.

Destroy the mark.

Do not preserve the object for study.

The effect normally diminishes within several hours.

Existing threats do not disappear.

A criminal already travelling toward a marked object will not necessarily turn around.

A fire already burning will continue to burn.

A creature already present remains present.

Containment therefore prevents **additional convergence**; it does not reverse events already initiated.

## Copies

Exact reproduction does not appear necessary.

Hand-drawn versions have activated.

Partial markings usually do not.

The threshold separating active from inactive representations remains poorly defined.

For this reason, archival material avoids displaying even heavily altered versions.

**UMB-033 DOCUMENT CONTROL**

Do not trace the mark.

Do not reconstruct missing sections.

Do not test remembered versions.

Do not reproduce it as decoration.

Do not mark another object in an attempt to redirect an existing convergence event.

The final prohibition was added following Incident UMB-033-18.

## Ulveth

No physical manifestation of Ulveth has ever been confirmed.

Whether a creature corresponding to UMB-033 exists is unknown.

Historical traditions nevertheless describe the rune as belonging to an entity variously translated as:

**The Invitation**

**The Open Hand**

**The Caller of Wolves**

**The Door Left Unlocked**

and:

**That Which Sends What You Deserve**

The last title has led to the widespread belief that Ulveth judges its victims.

Research does not support this.

Innocent and malicious subjects appear equally vulnerable.

## Current Status

UMB-033 is classified:

**ACTIVE — INFORMATION-ASSOCIATED**

All known controlled reproductions have been destroyed.

Unauthorised examples are presumed to remain in circulation.

No complete inventory is possible.

**ENCOUNTER GUIDANCE // UMB-033**

If an object is suspected of bearing the UMB-033 mark:

**DO NOT TRANSPORT IT THROUGH POPULATED AREAS.**

**DO NOT SELL OR TRANSFER OWNERSHIP.**

**DO NOT CREATE A COPY FOR IDENTIFICATION PURPOSES.**

Destroy or completely remove the marking where safe to do so.

Remain alert for threats already drawn to the location.

If unrelated adverse events begin occurring in rapid succession:

ASSUME CONVERGENCE IS ALREADY ACTIVE.

> It does not curse the house.
> It tells everything terrible where the house is.
>
> — UMB-033 field memorandum

name: Vaelkr
summary: The Rain-Strider: an immense, emaciated Umbuso seen walking Skgurr's coastal waters in heavy rain.
body:
*Possible depiction of UMB-063 off the coast of Skgurr. Date and exact location withheld.*

**Vaelkr**, commonly known as **the Rain-Strider**, is an [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md) associated with the coastline of Skgurr.

Reports describe an immense, emaciated organism walking through coastal waters during periods of heavy rain.

No reliable account describes Vaelkr arriving.

No reliable account describes Vaelkr leaving.

It is simply noticed somewhere along the coast.

**ARCHIVAL NOTICE**

The name *Vaelkr* originates from an old coastal Skgurr dialect.

Early translations rendered the word approximately as:

*one who walks beneath bad weather.*

A second translation was removed from circulation following Incident ██████.

## Overview

Vaelkr is one of the few known Umbuso whose appearances demonstrate a consistent environmental pattern.

It is seen almost exclusively during storms.

Witnesses describe a towering dark organism moving parallel to the shoreline, usually several hundred metres from land.

Its body remains partially submerged even in water known to be considerably deeper than its visible limbs should allow.

Vaelkr appears capable of walking normally regardless of water depth, seabed composition or wave conditions.

It has never been conclusively observed swimming.

It does not cross the sea.

It walks through it.

## Appearance

Vaelkr possesses an extremely tall, narrow body supported by several elongated limbs.

The upper body is skeletal in appearance, with branching structures extending from the head and shoulders.

These structures have been compared to antlers, exposed bone and dead coastal trees.

Two luminous white eyes are visible upon the head.

No mouth has been conclusively identified.

The lower portion of Vaelkr is obscured by long, dark structures hanging from its body.

Whether these structures are fur, tissue, vegetation or something else entirely remains unknown.

When Vaelkr moves, they drag through the sea without visibly responding to currents or waves.

## Behaviour

Vaelkr follows the coastline.

This behaviour appears simple.

It is not.

Historical records spanning several centuries describe the creature travelling in the same general direction during every confirmed appearance.

No account exists of Vaelkr reversing direction.

No account exists of Vaelkr reaching a destination.

No known coastline is long enough to accommodate the distances implied by surviving reports.

Attempts to continuously track the entity have failed.

During observation, Vaelkr may remain visible for minutes or several hours.

Heavy rain frequently obscures the creature.

When observers regain visual contact, it may be kilometres farther along the coast.

Occasionally it is simply gone.

## Storm Association

Vaelkr has never been reliably documented beneath clear skies.

Most sightings occur during:

- prolonged rainfall;
- severe coastal storms;
- unusually low cloud;
- rough seas;
- sudden drops in temperature;
- or periods of dense fog immediately preceding rain.

It remains uncertain whether Vaelkr causes these conditions or merely appears during them.

Weather records from several sightings indicate storms began before the entity was observed.

In two documented cases, however, rainfall continued around Vaelkr's estimated location after weather conditions elsewhere had cleared.

One storm persisted for ██ days.

## The Eyes

Vaelkr possesses two brilliant white eyes.

Their luminosity remains constant regardless of surrounding conditions.

Unlike reflected eyeshine, they appear to generate their own light.

They remain visible through rainfall and fog dense enough to completely obscure the creature's body.

Sailors have occasionally mistaken them for distant navigation lights.

This error has resulted in multiple vessels changing course toward the entity.

**MARITIME DIRECTIVE UMB-063-A**

During severe weather along the Skgurr coastline, paired white lights observed offshore must not be used for navigation.

If the lights remain level while waves obscure the horizon:

**TURN AWAY.**

Survivors of close encounters consistently report that the eyes illuminate nothing around them.

Rain crossing directly in front of the lights remains dark.

## Coastal Folklore

Stories resembling Vaelkr encounters occur throughout coastal Skgurr.

Older fishing communities possess numerous names for a tall figure observed beyond the surf.

Translations include:

- **The Long Fisher**
- **The Man Beyond the Breakers**
- **The Storm Walker**
- **The Empty Mast**
- **He Who Never Beaches**

Some communities traditionally extinguish harbour lights during particularly severe storms.

Today, this is often explained as an old practice intended to conserve fuel.

Older documents suggest otherwise.

*Do not light the harbour when the tall one passes.*

*A light from land tells him there is land.*

## Maritime Encounters

Ships account for several of the closest documented encounters with Vaelkr.

Reports are inconsistent.

Some crews describe passing within several hundred metres of the organism without receiving any apparent reaction.

Others report the creature turning its head toward the vessel.

Three surviving records describe Vaelkr reaching toward a ship.

Only one of those ships returned.

The surviving captain refused to provide a complete account.

The official transcript consists of seventeen pages.

Fourteen remain sealed.

The publicly available portion ends with the statement:

*It wasn't reaching for us.*

████████████████████████████████████████

## Depth Problem

Vaelkr frequently appears to stand in water which should be too deep for its visible anatomy.

This was initially attributed to inaccurate historical estimates of distance.

Modern observations have disproven that explanation.

During Observation UMB-063-11, Vaelkr was photographed approximately 1.7 kilometres offshore.

Recorded water depth at that position was 196 metres.

Based upon the visible proportions of the organism, its lower limbs should have extended approximately 32 metres beneath the surface.

Vaelkr nevertheless walked normally.

Sonar produced no reliable image of its submerged anatomy.

**OBSERVED HEIGHT ABOVE WATER:** 47 m

**EXPECTED SUBMERGED LENGTH:** 32 m

**RECORDED SEABED DEPTH:** 196 m

**METHOD OF LOCOMOTION:** UNKNOWN

One researcher proposed that Vaelkr's limbs do not terminate where its visible anatomy suggests.

The hypothesis was withdrawn.

The original report is no longer publicly accessible.

## The Coastline

No confirmed Vaelkr sighting has occurred away from the sea.

This has led to speculation that the entity may be physically incapable of leaving the coastline.

There is no evidence supporting this assumption.

Researchers are specifically warned against treating the shore as a protective boundary.

Several historical stories describe enormous footprints discovered above the high-tide line after major storms.

No verified photograph exists.

One plaster cast was reportedly produced in ████.

Its current location is unknown.

## Incident UMB-063-07

On ████████, a coastal observation team tracked Vaelkr for approximately six hours during severe rainfall.

The entity remained between 900 metres and 1.4 kilometres offshore.

**03:17** — UMB-063 stopped moving.

**03:19** — all six observers reported that the entity had turned to face inland.

Video footage was obscured by rain.

**03:26** — one observer reported seeing the eyes above the observation station rather than offshore.

The remaining personnel disputed this.

**03:31** — communications failed.

████████████████████████████████████████████████████

██████████████████████████████████

The station was recovered empty two days later.

There was no evidence of structural damage.

Vaelkr was no longer visible.

## Relationship with Axius

Vaelkr produces relatively little measurable interference with Axius at long range.

At closer distances, effects become increasingly unpredictable.

Reported phenomena include:

- incorrect perception of water depth;
- inability to distinguish sea from sky;
- sounds appearing to originate beneath the observer;
- persistent sensations of walking despite remaining stationary;
- and Axius manifestations orienting toward the sea without instruction.

One practitioner exposed during Incident ████ repeatedly stated:

*It thinks the coast is moving.*

No accepted interpretation exists.

## Current Status

Vaelkr remains officially classified as:

**ACTIVE — LOCATION UNKNOWN**

The most recent confirmed sighting occurred somewhere along the Skgurr coastline in ████.

Unverified reports continue.

Most coincide with poor weather and cannot be confirmed.

Archive policy prohibits deliberate attempts to locate UMB-063.

**LAST VERIFIED COASTAL REPORT**

21:03 — severe rainfall

21:11 — possible visual contact offshore

21:14 — two white lights confirmed

21:18 — UMB-063 classification probable

21:26 — entity moving north

22:09 — entity still moving north

23:44 — entity still moving north

01:17 — ██████████████████

01:18 — observers ordered inland

The final recorded position placed Vaelkr approximately ████ kilometres beyond the northernmost point of the mapped coastline.

The discrepancy remains unresolved.

**ENCOUNTER GUIDANCE // UMB-063**

During storms on the Skgurr coast:

**Do not approach unidentified figures offshore.**

**Do not navigate toward paired white lights.**

**Do not attempt to follow Vaelkr along the coastline.**

**Do not assume remaining on land guarantees safety.**

If the entity stops walking:

LEAVE THE COAST IMMEDIATELY.

> When the rain hides the horizon, count the lights.
> If there are two, go home.
>
> — Skgurr coastal proverb

name: Veyrath
summary: The Black Saint: a never-clearly-seen Umbuso silhouette standing above Ordon's industrial skylines.
body:
*Reconstruction based upon multiple sightings above an industrial district of [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md). No verified photograph has revealed additional anatomical detail.*

**Veyrath**, known throughout parts of [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md) as **the Black Saint**, is an [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md) associated with dense urban centres, industrial districts and prolonged atmospheric pollution.

Unlike other documented Umbuso, Veyrath has never been clearly observed.

Every known sighting presents the entity in exactly the same manner:

**as a black silhouette against the sky.**

No face has been seen.

No skin has been described.

No reliable account has identified where its body begins or ends.

Only the lights remain consistent.

**ARCHIVAL NOTE UMB-084-A**

Do not refer to recovered imagery as photographs *of Veyrath*.

Current evidence does not establish that the silhouette represents the physical appearance of UMB-084.

Use:

**“photograph containing a UMB-084 manifestation.”**

## Overview

Veyrath is associated almost exclusively with the cities of [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md), particularly districts dominated by dense gothic architecture, heavy industry, foundries, elevated machinery and old steam infrastructure.

Witnesses typically notice the entity above the skyline.

It appears enormously tall.

Its upper body is irregular and branching, commonly interpreted as possessing multiple heads, horns, limbs or tendrils.

Descriptions are inconsistent.

Illustrations are inconsistent.

Photographs are inconsistent.

The silhouette itself is not.

Nobody has ever seen what Veyrath looks like.

People have only seen the shape which says that Veyrath is there.

## Appearance

Descriptions of Veyrath's anatomy are considered unreliable.

The entity appears as a complete absence of visible detail.

Its body is darker than surrounding structures even when viewed at night.

Artificial illumination does not reveal texture.

Searchlights directed toward the silhouette have failed to produce reflected light.

Lightning behind the entity increases the clarity of its outline without exposing any internal features.

Observers commonly describe:

- several elongated upper appendages;
- between three and seven apparent heads;
- a large central mass;
- narrow structures resembling arms;
- curling projections resembling tails or smoke;
- and numerous white lights embedded within the silhouette.

No two anatomical diagrams agree.

This is not solely the result of poor visibility.

During simultaneous observations from different locations, witnesses have reported **different outlines**.

## The Silhouette Condition

The inability to observe Veyrath directly is known as the **Silhouette Condition**.

It persists regardless of distance, weather or method of observation.

Known attempts include:

- optical telescopes;
- industrial searchlights;
- photographic plates;
- high-speed cameras;
- thermal imaging;
- airborne observation;
- Axius-enhanced vision;
- and direct observation from neighbouring rooftops.

All have failed.

Equipment capable of detecting surrounding buildings normally records those buildings without issue.

The region occupied by Veyrath appears as featureless darkness.

**VISIBLE SURFACE DETAIL:** 0

**THERMAL SIGNATURE:** NONE

**REFLECTED LIGHT:** NONE

**KNOWN MASS:** UNKNOWN

**CONFIRMED PHYSICAL BODY:** UNRESOLVED

Researchers initially assumed that smoke or atmospheric pollution concealed the entity.

This theory was abandoned following Manifestation UMB-084-12.

The air was completely clear.

The silhouette remained.

## The Lights

Veyrath contains several points of intense white light.

These are the only features ever observed within the silhouette.

They are usually interpreted as eyes.

This interpretation is not officially recognised.

The number varies.

Most sightings contain between eight and fourteen.

Several historical illustrations show significantly more.

The lights sometimes appear in pairs.

At other times, their arrangement shows no obvious biological symmetry.

**OBSERVATION UMB-084-06**

Observer A reports 11 lights.

Observer B reports 8 lights.

Observer C reports 14 lights.

Photographic plate contains 9.

All observations made simultaneously.

██████████████████████████████████████████

Do not attempt reconciliation.

There is no evidence that these lights serve as visual organs.

Nevertheless, witnesses frequently report the impression of being watched.

## Smoke

Veyrath sightings have historically been associated with industrial smoke.

The oldest Ordon records refer to enormous shapes glimpsed between chimney stacks during periods of intense factory activity.

For generations, the phenomenon was dismissed as smoke distortion.

The discovery of older accounts complicated this explanation.

Descriptions resembling Veyrath exist from centuries before Ordon industrialised.

Those accounts describe:

*a black congregation above the chimneys of winter.*

No chimneys existed in the recorded settlement at the time.

The original manuscript contains an illustration.

The architecture depicted resembles modern Ordon.

██████████████████████████████████████████████████

The document has been removed from public exhibition.

## Behaviour

Veyrath has never been observed performing conventional locomotion.

It does not walk.

It does not fly.

It does not climb.

Its location simply changes.

During manifestations lasting several hours, Veyrath may appear behind one section of skyline and later be observed elsewhere.

No transition has been documented.

Witnesses who maintain uninterrupted visual contact frequently insist that the creature has not moved.

Observers elsewhere simultaneously report it in a different location.

Both reports may be correct.

Never attempt to determine which building Veyrath is standing behind.

This instruction appears in Ordon folklore centuries before formal Umbuso research began.

Its significance remains unclear.

## The Skyline Rule

One of the most consistent features of UMB-084 manifestations is Veyrath's relationship with architecture.

The entity is almost always observed **behind** structures.

Chimneys.

Church spires.

Clock towers.

Factory stacks.

Bridges.

Cranes.

Rooftops.

Even when observers relocate, Veyrath continues to appear behind the skyline from their perspective.

Attempts to physically approach the supposed position of the entity have therefore produced contradictory results.

An observer may estimate Veyrath to be two kilometres away.

Another, viewing from the opposite side of the district, may also place it two kilometres away.

Both describe the entity as being behind the buildings between them.

**FIELD NOTE**

We reached the street where it should have been standing.

Nothing was there.

We turned around.

It was behind the building we'd just left.

The team responsible for this observation immediately terminated the investigation.

## Architecture of Ordon

Some historians believe Veyrath influenced the development of traditional Ordon architecture.

Older districts frequently contain:

- excessively tall spires;
- narrow towers;
- crowded rooflines;
- decorative iron frameworks;
- bridges between buildings;
- elaborate chimney structures;
- and sightlines intentionally interrupted by architectural features.

The conventional explanation is aesthetic.

Several recovered construction documents suggest another purpose.

A design specification dated ████ repeatedly instructs architects:

**NEVER ALLOW AN UNBROKEN VIEW OF THE WESTERN SKY.**

No explanation is provided.

Similar instructions have been discovered in plans for churches, railway stations and factories.

## The Black Saint

The title **Black Saint** originates in working-class districts of industrial Ordon.

During the height of early industrialisation, workers occasionally reported an enormous dark figure standing beyond factory roofs.

The phenomenon became associated with industrial accidents.

According to surviving folklore, seeing the Black Saint before beginning a shift meant that someone would not return home.

Factory owners publicly discouraged the superstition.

Privately, several facilities suspended operations following reported sightings.

One surviving notice states:

**FOUNDRY CLOSED UNTIL MONDAY**

Atmospheric conditions unsuitable.

Machinery undergoing inspection.

Do not ring the upper bell.

The final instruction appears only on the handwritten original.

## Bells

Veyrath possesses an unexplained association with bells.

Church bells, factory shift bells and clock towers have all reportedly malfunctioned during manifestations.

Common reports include:

- bells ringing without mechanical movement;
- clocks striking incorrect hours;
- bells producing no sound despite visible movement;
- multiple towers ringing simultaneously;
- and bells being heard from structures which possess none.

During UMB-084-08, seventeen clock towers across central Ordon rang thirteen times at precisely 02:11.

Only four contained functional bells.

Veyrath was photographed above the eastern industrial district nine minutes later.

**ORDON MUNICIPAL DIRECTIVE // UMB-084**

During a suspected UMB-084 manifestation:

Do not investigate unexplained bells.

Do not enter bell towers.

Do not attempt manual correction of malfunctioning clock mechanisms.

If a clock strikes **thirteen**:

Leave the building.

## Incident UMB-084-09

Incident UMB-084-09 represents the closest known attempt to physically approach a manifestation.

At 22:14, Veyrath was observed behind an abandoned foundry complex.

A research team entered the district from the south.

The entity remained visible throughout the approach.

**22:31** — estimated distance: 840 metres.

**22:38** — estimated distance: 390 metres.

**22:44** — estimated distance: 170 metres.

**22:47** — team reached the foundry.

No entity located.

Observers stationed outside the district continued to see Veyrath.

Their estimated distance remained approximately 2.4 kilometres.

**22:51** — field team reported hearing bells.

There were no bells within the foundry complex.

**22:53** — ██████████████████████

**22:54** — external observers reported change in UMB-084 silhouette.

**22:55** — number of visible lights increased from eleven to ████.

**22:57** — field communications ceased.

██████████████████████████████████████████████████

██████████████████████████████████████

The foundry was demolished six months later.

Official documentation cites structural instability.

The basement was filled with concrete before demolition began.

## Recorded Images

Hundreds of photographs purportedly depicting Veyrath exist.

Most are fraudulent, misidentified smoke formations or conventional atmospheric effects.

Approximately ██ remain unexplained.

Confirmed imagery shares a peculiar property.

Image enhancement reveals additional detail in:

- buildings;
- clouds;
- smoke;
- machinery;
- rainfall;
- birds;
- and distant terrain.

It never reveals additional detail within Veyrath.

Increasing exposure produces a brighter environment surrounding the silhouette.

The silhouette remains black.

One researcher described the phenomenon as:

*It isn't underexposed.*

*There is simply no image there.*

## Witness Disagreement

Witness accounts of Veyrath contradict one another more severely than those of most Umbuso.

Observers disagree about:

- number of heads;
- number of limbs;
- height;
- orientation;
- distance;
- position;
- and whether the entity was moving.

They almost universally agree on three details.

It was black.

There were lights inside it.

They knew they were looking at something alive.

Why that certainty is so consistent remains unexplained.

## Relationship with Axius

Axius displays unusual perceptual effects around UMB-084 manifestations.

No direct suppression has been documented.

Instead, Axius users frequently report becoming aware of architectural spaces which should not exist.

Examples include:

- additional floors in buildings;
- windows visible only from certain streets;
- staircases continuing above the top floor;
- doors appearing between adjacent buildings;
- chimneys extending significantly farther upward than physically possible;
- and silhouettes visible through solid walls.

These effects disappear after manifestations end.

One Axius practitioner claimed to have followed a staircase upward for approximately forty minutes.

The building contained six floors.

When recovered, the practitioner was found on the ground floor.

They refused to explain what was at the top.

## Current Status

Veyrath is classified:

**ACTIVE — INTERMITTENT**

Unlike several known Umbuso, no specific territory can be sealed around UMB-084.

Manifestations occur within populated areas.

Major evacuations are therefore rarely feasible.

Modern Ordon maintains automated atmospheric and visual monitoring throughout several industrial districts.

The system primarily searches for simultaneous reports involving:

- unexplained white lights;
- silhouette anomalies;
- abnormal bell activity;
- contradictory distance measurements;
- and visual obstructions appearing above the skyline.

The most recent confirmed manifestation occurred in ████.

It lasted approximately thirteen minutes.

No casualties were officially recorded.

**AUTOMATED VISUAL LOG**

01:02 — skyline normal

01:03 — skyline normal

01:04 — silhouette detected

01:05 — object classification failed

01:06 — object classification failed

01:07 — 12 light sources detected

01:08 — 14 light sources detected

01:09 — 17 light sources detected

01:10 — ████████████████

01:11 — skyline normal

Manual review subsequently identified the silhouette in images recorded from 00:41 onward.

**ENCOUNTER GUIDANCE // UMB-084**

If a large silhouette is observed above the Ordon skyline:

**Remain indoors.**

**Do not attempt to improve your viewing angle.**

**Do not travel toward the apparent position of the entity.**

**Do not enter towers, rooftops or elevated walkways to observe it.**

**Ignore unexplained bells.**

Do not attempt to determine what Veyrath looks like.

If the silhouette disappears while you are still looking at it:

DO NOT TURN AROUND.

> When the Saint stands above the chimneys, keep your eyes on the street.
>
> — Old Ordon saying

name: Kelemvor
summary: God of the Dead and judge of the damned. An Old God whose name is really a title, passed from one deserving dead mortal to the next. Five holders are known.
body:
## Overview

Kelemvor is one of the few death gods who believes that death should be honoured, not used as a tool. He acts as the judge of the damned, sending those who have passed on to their appropriate final resting place. He is an Old God, but willing to swap sides to gain more power. Many of the other gods "don't get them". Each Kelemvor tends to associate with different gods, but the most common company is [Hermod](/content/deities/hermod.md) and [Chauntea](/content/deities/chauntea.md).

Kelemvor is less a god than a title. The role passes to deserving mortals when they die, and the new Death is often groomed before taking its place. Some mortals don't know this, but a god of death who never died doesn't make any sense. The first Kelemvors are lost to time; five are known.

## Motivation and philosophy

Kelemvor's motivation is very simple. They believe death should be an honoured tradition, and despise it when other gods use it for personal gain or for their beliefs. They do not willingly socialise with others.

## The holders of the title

### Abernath: the Grasping Passage

Abernath believed he was above impunity. He was the first being ever to die in the world, a bitter old man, and was forced into the role of Kelemvor, although the term hadn't been coined yet. Cold and calculating, he prided himself on his self-taught merit. As the forefounder of all the Dead Gods, he was woefully mishandled, bitter and ineffective, and he left no lasting legacy.

Because no ceremony for transferring the power had been created, there was no handover. When his estranged daughter Dianye died, her soul was held in [Carceri](/content/locations/carceri.md) until Abernath relinquished the position, and she then had to take on his workload. Only when Dianye was finally able to control her newfound godhood could the Cognitive Age begin, ending the Grasping Passage.

### Dianye: 0 CA

Dianye lived a very normal life. There was nothing special about her, apart from the fact that her father was Death; he had abandoned her while he was still mortal. On her ascension, instead of a peaceful afterlife, she found a whole new series of struggles had followed her. She worked out what had happened to her by pulling her father back to life and speaking with him directly. Breathing life back into him was a sacrilegious act. Abernath was of no use: Dianye asked for help, he refused to support her, and the two bickered often. Disgusted but determined, Dianye realised she was trapped for the rest of eternity.

Her powers didn't come close to Abernath's, and she realised she had her work cut out for her. Carving out her own space inside her own realm, she created an institution to work hard. It took thousands of years to create a sustainable environment where she could work, but she brought the Grasping Passage to an end. She is depicted as the very first aasimar.

In a cruel twist of fate, just as Dianye was beginning to feel comfortable in her position, she began ageing, her powers dwindling and her mind fading. She spent her last few hundred years recording all she knew, and set about transferring her power to a mortal she believed was worthy. It was she who created the title Kelemvor.

### Carvell: 6,924 CA

Carvell was a man of the law. Inspired by his father, he went out to make a difference in the world. Within his first year of service he was killed protecting a family from outlaws, and his own father held his body as he died. Dianye saw the purity of his heart, and knew this tragedy could still have a somewhat happier ending.

Carvell was taken and given full power. The transfer was simple and easy, and Carvell worked to reinforce and build on what Dianye had founded. When his father's time came, instead of bringing him to death, Carvell employed him to help with his duties, free to retire at any point. But the years took their toll on Carvell, and he felt guilt for those he transported. So the seed was sown for the next Kelemvor.

### Wernicke: the Lingering Silence

Wernicke was an executioner of the Cognitive Age who died by mistake. Carvell chose him for his clear-headedness while performing executions, but after the transfer the two famously hated each other. They had completely different views of the role: Carvell wanted it to be an honourable, neutral and homely experience, while Wernicke wanted it efficient but cold. They argued often, and tensions ran high as Carvell knew his time was up. As a kind of revenge, Wernicke ushered in the Lingering Silence, showing how bad he could make the world if he chose.

Eventually Wernicke realised how spiteful he had been. He tried to resurrect his master so he could redo his studies and learn how to be a good Kelemvor, but instead he was met by Dianye. She comforted him and taught him anew. They worked together for many years, and Wernicke ended up serving a very long time, proud of how far he had come.

Then the Oblate happened, and for the first time in centuries Kelemvor's powers were out of their hands. The sheer amount of death strained their powers, and they quickly lost control. Seeing how the world that had been so well maintained had fallen, and how he had let down everyone (Carvell, Dianye), Wernicke killed himself.

### Mort: 2 AO

Mort was as standard as standard could be. Sold from his family's farm to help pay debts to Thevethalas, he became a pirate with the Bilgewater Rats. After he died, he was chosen to become the Kelemvor. Upon researching his new position, Mort took on Dianye's new role…

*(The source text stops here.)*

## Worship

- **Mourcroft** (Maillon, Thevethalas) grew up around a gravesite and became one of the main sites of Kelemvor worship. Locals say its mist is a blessing from Kelemvor, marking it as one of the places closest to the realm of Death. Its High Lord, Cenric Mourbraith, comes from a long line of death-priests and holds strong influence over the Priesthood of Kelemvor.

## GM notes

- Name spellings in the sources: Abernath (v3), Abernathe or Abernate (v2).
- The holy symbol is blank in the source.
- v3 called Kelemvor a "Scion". The user chose v2: an Old God (2026-11-04). v3's additions to Dianye's story (held in Carceri; resurrecting her father) were kept at the user's request.
- "Kelemvor's Host" is noted in v2 as a placeholder name ("get better names").

name: Aureluch
summary: Ordon's great cliffside rail-and-freight city, the interchange that binds the country's trade together.

fields.major_industries: Rail freight, metalworking, engineering and Morrow refinement
fields.major_transport: Rail, chain-lifts, freight hoists and cliff roads

body:
**Aureluch** is one of the largest industrial cities in [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md) outside [Morgenwelde](/content/locations/morgenwelde.md). Half built into a cliff face and half stretching across the lowlands, the city consists of rail-yards, foundries, lift-chains, suspended neighbourhoods and vertical engines connected by an enormous network of gates and bridges. It is the city that **binds Ordon together**.

Passengers, grain from the outer regions, military freight, machinery and Morrow fuel all pass through the city on their way to trade, to the capital, to the coast, or just to another city.

Its importance is not based upon political authority or cultural prestige, but upon infrastructure. A disruption in Aureluch can delay trade across much of Ordon, and thus the world.

## Overview

Aureluch developed around a natural break in the cliffs separating Ordon's inland provinces from the lower western routes. What began as a fortified crossing and freight station gradually expanded into one of the country's largest transport centres.

The city is divided into two halves, **cliffside** and **groundside**. Cliffside consists of smaller districts and observatory posts, as well as major passenger lines. Groundside consists of stations, rail-lines and most housing. It is commonplace to see Thunderrails being lifted cliffside for inspection and boarding.

Movement through Aureluch depends upon:

- Chain-driven lifts
- Suspended walkways
- Freight platforms
- Rail bridges
- Cliff tunnels
- Mechanical gates
- Inclined railways
- Stairways cut directly into the rock

## Geography and layout

Aureluch occupies both sides of a steep ravine known as the **Aureluch Cut**. The oldest districts are carved into the cliffs, while newer neighbourhoods have been constructed on platforms, bridge foundations and suspended frames.

## History

### The Old Crossing

Before Aureluch became a city, the ravine contained one of the few reliable routes through the surrounding cliffs. Early settlements maintained bridges, toll gates and storage houses for merchants travelling between inland Ordon and the coast. Its beauty and danger made it a landmark for traders.

### Discovery of Morrow

The industrial importance of the settlement increased following the widespread use of Morrow. The ore could be transported from inland mines to the crossing, refined locally and then moved towards Morgenwelde or the coast.

The first large foundries were established near the base of the ravine, where water and cliffside tunnels made heavy construction possible.

### The Railway Expansion

Aureluch grew rapidly after the construction of Ordon's national railway network.

Existing roads and bridges could not handle the volume of freight passing through the city. Engineers responded by building new rail levels above the old settlement, followed by lifts capable of moving entire freight wagons between elevations.

Aureluch's population increased as workers arrived from across Ordon.

### The Binding of Ordon

The completion of the **Grand Junction** transformed Aureluch into the central interchange of Ordon's freight network.

Grain from rural provinces, ore from inland mines, military equipment, coastal imports and Morrow fuel could now be redirected through a single city.

### Recent history

Aureluch continues to expand, although much of its oldest infrastructure is under severe strain.

## Districts

Working ideas for the city's districts:

- **Crown Station**: largest passenger terminal and administrative centre. Known for its clocks and cleanliness.
- **Grand Junction**: centre of the rail network, across several levels.
- **Chainward**: the lift-engine area.
- **Hanging Rows**: residential neighbourhoods suspended from reinforced cliff frames.
- **Blackgate**: controls the largest western freight entrance into Aureluch.
- **Furnace Deep**: contains Aureluch's heaviest foundries and oldest Morrow refineries.
- **Old Steps**: remains of the settlement that existed before the railways.
- **Underspan**: occupies the spaces beneath the largest bridges and freight platforms. Dangerous.

## Transport links

Aureluch is the most important transport interchange in Ordon outside the capital.

### Railways

The city connects several major railway routes:

- The **Morgwen Line** carries passengers, officials and manufactured goods to the capital.
- The **Inland Ore Line** transports raw Morrow and other minerals from Ordon's mining regions.
- The **Harvest Line** carries grain, livestock and preserved food from the outer provinces.
- The **Western Line** connects Aureluch to coastal ports.
- The **Military Spur** serves fortified depots and is restricted to authorised traffic.
- The **Highland Line** passes towards Ordon's northern settlements.

Most long-distance freight entering central Ordon passes through at least one Aureluch yard.

### Vertical engines

Aureluch's vertical engines move freight and passengers between the city's different elevations.

The largest can lift entire railway wagons. Smaller lifts transport workers, livestock and goods between neighbourhoods.

Lift access is controlled through gates, schedules and tolls. Breakdowns can leave whole districts temporarily isolated.

### Bridges

The city contains hundreds of bridges, ranging from small footbridges to enormous rail structures. Several major bridges contain buildings, markets and service roads along their length.

Important crossings include Union Bridge, Morrow Span, Founders' Crossing, The Nine Chains and the Grand Freight Bridge.

### Air travel

Aureluch maintains a limited airship platform at Crown Level.

The difficult winds around the ravine make airship travel unreliable. Most commercial and military traffic therefore continues to use rail.

## Economy and industry

Aureluch's economy is built around movement, storage and processing.

The city does not produce most of the goods that pass through it. Instead, it profits from controlling where those goods go.

The city is also a major centre for scrap dealing. Damaged machinery, broken rail components and rejected industrial materials are repaired or repurposed throughout the lower districts.

## Government

Aureluch is governed by a municipal council composed of civic officials, railway representatives, industrial owners and engineers. The council is commonly called the **Gate Council**.

The position of **First Gatekeeper** serves as the city's senior civic office. The title originated when the settlement was controlled through a single fortified crossing.

## Law and crime

The **Aureluch Gatewatch** is responsible for public order, freight inspection and transport security.

Smuggling is widespread due to the enormous volume of goods moving through the city. Contraband is hidden inside legitimate cargo, abandoned tunnels and unofficial lift systems.

The Underspan and Blackgate contain the city's largest criminal networks.

## Notable locations

- **Crown Station**: Aureluch's principal passenger terminal.
- **Grand Junction**: the centre of the national freight network.
- **The Nine Chains**: a series of enormous lift mechanisms spanning the ravine.
- **Union Bridge**: one of the city's oldest inhabited bridges.
- **Gate Council Hall**: the seat of Aureluch's municipal government.
- **The Last Lantern**: a well-known inn used by railway workers and travellers.
- **Furnace Twelve**: a major Morrow refinery with a troubled safety record.
- **The Silent Platform**: an abandoned station whose original destination has been removed from official records.

## GM notes

- Crown Station "needs renaming".
- Railway lines: "THESE NAMES ARE ALL PLACEHOLDERS I NEED TO CHANGE THEM AND DESIGN A FUN RAIL NETWORK". (The Morgwen Line is named after the capital's older name.)
- Population: to be determined.
- The wiki page has a splash image, a city map and four visual-reference images (rail yards, lower city, bridges, foundry). None of them have been uploaded to the wiki yet.

name: Carceri
summary: A prison sub-realm of Limbo, created by a pact of the Old Gods for beings who rival or offend them. It is the first demi-plane, and being locked in it is the greatest sentence in the universe.
body:
Sometime after creation, an interplanar bargain was struck between the Old Gods: there would be those who rival their power, who offend them, who challenge them. They would need a place to teach these beings a lesson, because death was not final enough.

A pact was created: as long as no god opposed it, any such creation would be sent to a new creation, Carceri, a sub-realm of [Limbo](/content/locations/limbo.md). This technically makes it the first demi-plane, predating the others by epochs.

Moulded like a whirlpool at the centre of Limbo, it ironically forms the largest coherent landmass in the plane. A multitude of beings dwell there, often as powerful as gods, but without their mercy. To be locked in Carceri is the greatest sentence known to the universe.

## Known prisoners

- Dianye, before she became [Kelemvor](/content/deities/kelemvor.md): her soul was held here until her father Abernath gave up the role of Death.

## GM notes

- Reference art used in the v3 note: "Ice of Carceri" by Dawn Carlos (Forgotten Realms wiki). It is third-party art, so it isn't stored here.

Heresy is one of the oldest and most respected places in Halingo, so much so it could be described as one of the only cities in the region. Two-Hundred years ago, a warlock known as Seneth of Draugr declared war on the (at the time) small town, declaring it to be his target of holy war. His follower’s attacked the city overnight, with only three members of law enforcement being able to defend their home.. Their names were Rael, Garrus and Corrin. Rael and Garrus were the deputy and Sheriff respectively, and had been married for some time. Corrin was their adoptive son, who had previously adventured with Seneth, but split after realising the true nature of his companion. In the fight, Garrus passed, supposedly bringing Rael to surrender. Corrin though, remained. 

The two previous friends battled, even when all others gave up and died around them. Eventually, upon seeing the destruction and death around them, the two gave up. Some say both of them forever wander the desert, each seeking each other for a finale. Some say they walked away that day. Some say they died. All that is known is that they haven’t been seen again. All that is known that, a few years after the initial combat, Rael founded Heresy II (usually just referred to as Heresy) and alongside it, the Raincloaks, determined to never let what happened to his husband, happen again. 

These days, Heresy is a place of peace and prosperity. It has functioning mines, is connected via Thunderbolt network to larger settlements, has strict rules and is where many Raincloaks are trained.

#Category/Location #Locations #Limate #Capital

# Story
Khundur is one of the oldest cities in the known world

# Basic Information:
**Origin - First Settlement:** This city was the first recorded place Dwarf emerged from the underground.
**Age - Ancient**: The capital is older than recorded memory.
**Size - Very large**: The capital can support ~150,000 people.
**General condition - Impressive:** The capital is well taken care of, and cleanliness is clearly a priority.
**Fortification - Extreme**: The capital is surrounded with stone walls, with many staffed watchtowers. The gate is massive, reinforced with iron bands, augmented with a polcullis and is always manned. Nothing goes in or out without the watch's knowledge or permission.

# Districts:
**4 total districts:**
**Arcane**. Magnificent condition. It is open and unguarded. Crime is infrequent.
Contains:
- Grand Library
- Academy
- A magic shop for clothing / armour
- A magic shop for wonderous items
- Magic mercanaries
- Barber
- Tavern
There are two notable locations: Firstly, a club, 'Magi Infernus' which is known for its generosity. Secondly is an alchemist, Skjur which has odd rumours of experimentation and live testing.

**Khundur Market**. Impressive condition. It is gated and guarded. Crime is common.
Contains:
- Baker
- Butcher
- General Store
- Magic Item Shop
- Smithy
- Tailor
- Tavern
There are two notable locations: Firstly, a Rare Trade Goods (shop) which is a common meeting place due to its exotic appearance. Secondly, a Hired Help - Caravan & Mount which has large advertising campaigns throughout the city.

Contains:

- Inn
- Stable
There are two notable locations: Apothecary, which always seems to have some insane injury or event occurring. An artist, which is renowned for her services and her wife, who plays beautiful pieces whilst you wait and watch them work. This also hides the Zhentarim HQ.

**Temple of Gond**. Impressive condition. It is guarded. Crime is common.
Contains:
- Temple
- Library
- Scribes
- Priestly Guidance
- Hands of the Divine (divine magic in combat)
There is one notable location which is a bathhouse which is also a front for a strip area / drug dealing area.

# Government and High Society:
**Leadership: Hereditary**
**Governing Priority: Control**
**Priority approach: Aggressive (Moderate)**. A defensive stance is taken, though opportunity is provided for good faith.
**Priority success: Very Sucessful.** The leadership has made great strides at achieving its inital vision.

**Leader Lifestyle: Humble.** The leader requires only what is nessisary to live and function basically.
**Residence: Small mansion.** The leader's residence likely has several spare rooms, as well as space for a recreational room or two.
**Intent: Genuine**

# Military:
The capital has its own standing military force. The members are conscripted, criminals, and handpicked, which form different regiments. It is a grand size.
The criminal regiments have access to highly experimental and deadly diseases/chemicals.
The conscripted regiments have simple structures inside the capital, but the handpicked have moderate structures outside the capital.

**Intelligence Gathering**: N/A. The capital is not engaged in any intelligence gathering operations.
**Counterintelligence**: Modest. The capital has up to a few operatives working within its borders.
**Counterintelligence Watchfullness**: Weary. Efforts are diligent and concerted.

# Community:
**Population density: Crowded.** The capital is filled with jostling throngs of people. Practically all structures are occupied. Bumping into people is difficult.
**Population wealth: Wealthy.** Nearly everyone has what they need to live comfortably, many are able to live well, and some are very prosperous.
**Visitor traffic: Groups.** There are a fair amount of vistors to the capital.
**Disposition: Open.** Since they are cleared by the city watch, it means they are to be trusted and embraced as if they live here.
**Night activity: Slow.** Almost everything is closed except for taverns.

# Crime & Law
**Law Enforcement: Robust City Watch.** Run by a captain and two sergeants, the watch are able to place extra support at key points, as well as establish 3 or 4 patrols a day.
**General crime: Frequent.** The streets are unsafe alone, and a purse in plain sight is destined to be stolen. Vandalism and muggings are fairly regular.
**Organised crime: Talk.** Enogu hincidents have occured that most folk don't have trouble believing there is an organised criminal element in the capital.

name: Limbo
summary: The Chaotic Neutral outer plane of pure, untamed creative chaos, where only willpower can impose order. It holds Carceri at its centre.
body:
Limbo is a realm of pure, untamed, creative chaos. It is the plane of raw potential, where the very substance of reality has not yet decided what it wants to be. The landscape is a terrifying, beautiful and utterly unpredictable storm of creation and dissolution. Continents of churning earth might rise from a sea of liquid ideas, only to crumble into a snowstorm. The "air" can be a breathable fog, a current of pure emotion, or a rain of molten paradoxes.

There are no laws here: not of physics, magic or society. The only force that matters is willpower. Beings of immense self-conviction can temporarily impose their will on the chaos, creating temporary islands of stability. Those with weak minds are torn apart, their very essence unravelled and repurposed as raw material for the Maelstrom. This is not a plane of good or evil; it is the ultimate expression of freedom, in both its creative and destructive forms.

## Key locations

- [Carceri](/content/locations/carceri.md): the prison demi-plane at Limbo's centre.

**Morgenwelde** is the capital of [Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md). It grew from the settlement [Quinten Hearspar](/content/locations/ordon.md#history) built around the **Eye of Gold**, and is the height of Ordonian technology. The details below use the *Spectacular Settlements* format.

## Overview

- **Origin:** Magical. The capital was founded around The Eye of Gold.
- **Age:** Old. The capital has been around for around 600 years. .
- **Size:** Very Large. The structures in the city can support over 150,000 people.

      - **Poor:** Dilapidated.

Visitors to the capital pass through a main gate that can be barred in the evenings. A few watch towers may be placed around the city, though are likely sporadic.
