- **Vendor Stall Acquisition:** Sponsered Referral Only - No Fee.
- **Merchant Overflow:** Unpatrolled. Excess vendors are allowed to set up stalls but, as the city watch do not patrol or monitor these areas, the risk is higher.
- **Underground Passages:** Sewers.

## Government & High Society

- **Leadership:** Oligarchy of Proctors
  - **Proctor of Causality:** Caius Valerius.
    - **Aspect of Control:** Caius is the one who attempts to divine the future using the equations of the Eyes of Brass equations. Sometimes, he is able to guide the city towards a stronger position, or at least, one more beneficial for him.
    - **Species:** Caius is actually an ancient, Axius augmented Illithid that entered the world after seeing Quinten break through the astral sea. Upon impact his body was deeply damaged, leading to him being permentantly ingrained into a massive throne/computer of brass wiring. Caius (Not his true name, is a moniker of the Illithid, as every other Proctor of Casuality before.)
    - **History:** Caius is the latest Proctor of Casuality, and as tradition, was picked from the city's divination researchers to become the next Proctor of Casuality. This is a complete fabriction. Caius never existed, and is just a way for the Illithid to keep up his role without drawing suspicion. As 'tradition' the new Proctor must remove himself from city life completely (yet another ruse to explain why they cannot be seen in public). The Caius seen on posters, advertisements and meetings is a simulacrum.
    - **Relationships:** He maintains a secret, transactional relationship with Lysander. He provides him with raw, real-time data from the underworld of the city.
  - **Proctor of Compliance:** General Klytuss.
    - **Aspect of Control:** The city Overseers and the state miltia. Klytuss is the iron fist that controls the city. Klytuss' whims are law and he controls the brutal police force in the city.
    - **Species:** A grim, battle-scarred, one-eyed Hobgoblin warlord, fused to his armour.
    - **History:** Klytuss is a sole survivor of a doomed trip to Morgau, which enabled him to establish the first Sunbeacon, preventing the spread of Contagion. He was granted a wish by the royal magistrates ring and chose to become a Proctor of Compliance - as was his committment to order.
    - **Relationships:** Klytuss utterly despises Lysander. If he had his way, the city would be run with an iron fist and no crime, apart from that he wants to happen, would occur. But the backroom dealings leave Klytuss' force often unaware of deals and crime.
      - Klytuss doesn't fully understand the point of Caius and will often refuse to help him, and deliberately ignore instructions. This is never to the level to form a genuine level of hatred, but it's certainly enough to note.
      - Klytuss has a buddy-buddy relationship with Hest. The somewhat always strained relationship between Hest needing more men, and Klytuss always needing more resources lead to a genuine bond, even if they can never fully give each other the resources they need.
  - **Proctor of Sanctity:** Matron Varhei
    - **Aspect of control:** The Regulators, religion and magical purity. Her goal is to hunt down all "Abominations" - unregistered magic users, seers, unlicensed religions and reality-glitches. She directs the fantatical Regulator order and ensures the states ideology remains clean.
    - **Spieces:** Air Genasi.
    - **History:** Varhei was a progidity within the Regulators, a witch-hunter of zeal and efficacy. She rose through the ranks by exposing a cabal of magic-users within her predecessor's own retinue, proving that no one was above suspicion. She is a true believer, utterly convinced of the righteousness of her cruel methods.
    - **Relationships:** Somewhat famous for despising everyone else, Varhei has but one exception. Klytuss. She is shamefully and sinfully in lust with him, and often goes 'soft' for his will, even if 'soft' for her, is still cold and diplomatic at best.
  - **Proctor of Logistics:** Hest Varsc
    - **Aspect of control:** Mines, Foundaries and Supply lines. Hest is the workhorse of the Council. He oversees the resource extraction from the Cragfall Mines and the industrial output of Morgenwelde. If the city stops eating or the army's forges go cold, it is his failure.
    - **Species:** An ancient **Dwarf**, his skin pale from a life spent underground and his long beard braided with humming Axius-powered wires that monitor the city's vital signs.
    - **History:** Hest's family has managed the deep engineering of Morgenwelde for centuries. He didn't rise to power through schemes or battle, but by becoming so essential to the city's operation that he could not be ignored. He is the oldest Proctor and has outlived dozens of his more volatile colleagues by simply being too difficult to replace.
    - **Relationships:** His strongest bond is with Klytuss. The somewhat always strained relationship between Hest needing more men, and Klytuss always needing more resources lead to a genuine bond, even if they can never fully give each other the resources they need. He respects Caius' information but not his methods, distruts Lysander's greed and weary of Varhei's fantasicsm. He is often the tie-breaking vote.
  - **Proctor of Acquisition:** Lysander Corvid
    - **Aspect of control:** Money, the black market, the guilds, and unofficial channels. Corvid is the spymaster from the gutter. He controls the criminal underworld, which he has reorganized into a ruthlessly efficient, state-sanctioned monopoly.
    - **Species:** A charismatic and unnervingly calm Yuan-Ti, always dressed in the finest silks, with subtle serpentine features visible to those who look too closely.
    - **History:** Lysander Corvid was once the most powerful crime lord in Morgenwelde. The Council spent decades trying to crush him. When they failed, they offered him a deal: a seat on the Council in exchange for bringing the entire underworld under his—and by extension, their—control. He accepted, effectively becoming the state's official racketeer.
    - **Relationships:** Despite them all hating him, Every other proctor uses his service. Klytuss uses his smugglers to bypass supply chain issues, Vorl uses his informants to find heretics, Hest contracts his non-union labor for dangerous jobs, and Valerius uses his spy network. Despite this, he is aware that if he went too far - the council could replace him.
- **Leadership Unity:** Close-Knit. Communication is open. Disagreements are constructive.
- **Governing Priority:** Industry & Innovation:
- **Diplomatic Approach:** Peaceful (Moderate). An agreeable stance is taken unless provoked, when an aggressive response is carefully deliberated.

## Lifestyle & Residence

### Caius Valerius

- **Lifestyle:** Exquisite + Humble. Caius has two homes. One is the home of Caius' simulacrum, the other is the Illithid's base of operations.
- **Residence:** Small Mansion + Modest House.

name: Ordon
summary: The largest and most influential country in Kurovia, an industrial oligarchy built on Morrow, its ore-form of Axius representing progress.

fields.major_exports: Steam machinery, processed and manufactured mass-produced goods, armour
fields.environment: A gloomy land of mist-shrouded mountains, steep gorges and dark forests.

body:
> Once upon a time, a coward made a wish. "I want to be important."

**Ordon** is the largest and most influential country in Kurovia. It is known for its industrial cities, steam-powered machinery, airships and the workable form of Axius found beneath its land.

Ordon's Axius manifestation represents the concept of **progress**. It can be refined into fuel, conductive machinery, armour and substances that increase human productivity. Although the country's capital possesses advanced technology, the settlements beyond its industrial centre increasingly resemble older and more traditional societies, deprived of the progress that so defines Central Ordon.

## Overview

Ordon is a country divided between rapid industrial development and older rural traditions. Its central cities are filled with factories, railways, workshops and Axius-powered technology, while its distant provinces remain dependent on agriculture, traditional crafts and local customs.

It is governed by an **Oligarchy of Proctors**, seated in the capital, [Morgenwelde](/content/locations/morgenwelde.md). Axius is tolerated.

## Geography

A gloomy land of mist-shrouded mountains, steep gorges and dark forests.

### Regions and provinces

- **Heartlands**: the industrial and political heart of the country.
- **Northern Ordon**: the colder, harsher and more independent portion of Ordon.
- **Lowlands**: large peasantlands, enjoying gentle weather and an easy climate.
- **Eastern Ordon**: primarily known for its transport city.
- **Western Ordon**: the "Frontier" of Ordon; many upstarts are found here.

### Climate

Ordon's climate is much like the real world, with strong seasonal effects. The summers are hot, the winters freezing.

Industrialised areas have light pollution, and the glow of the Barrier around the Eastern Area keeps many up at night.

### Natural resources

Ordon's most important natural resource is its regional form of Axius, **Morrow**, a malleable ore with different properties depending on how it is processed. Other resources include coal, iron, timber, agricultural land, stone and navigable rivers.

## Population

Ordon contains approximately **40%** of Kurovia's total population. Its inhabitants are unevenly distributed, with large numbers living in the capital and other industrial centres.

## Economy

Ordon possesses one of the most developed economies in Kurovia. Its wealth is closely connected to Axius mining, manufacturing and the production of advanced machinery.

Major industries:

- Axius mining and refinement
- Steam machinery
- Airship construction
- Armour and weapons
- Rail transport
- Pharmaceuticals and productivity drugs
- Agriculture
- Traditional rural crafts

## Axius in Ordon

Ordon's manifestation of Axius represents **progress**. It appears as a malleable ore that can be treated in several different ways.

### Fuel

When condensed, the ore becomes an energy source more powerful than coal. Much like coal, it also belches out fumes, at a much higher rate. The resulting energy is connected to the Weave.

### Conductive material

When treated lightly, Axius becomes highly conductive. This property has allowed Ordonian engineers to develop complex steam machinery and other advanced technologies.

### Armour

Ordon's strongest armour is manufactured from Axius ore. The armour provides exceptional protection, but prolonged use can create an attachment between the wearer and the metal.

Some wearers eventually become unable to remove it. This effect is not widely known among the public.

### Productivity drugs

Axius can be refined into a substance that increases concentration, energy and productivity.

## Technology

Ordon is the most technologically developed region of Kurovia, although this technology is not distributed evenly. The capital represents the height of Ordonian technology. Technology becomes less common further from the capital: smaller towns may possess rail connections and basic machinery, while remote villages continue to depend on traditional tools, animals and magic.

## Settlements

- **[Morgenwelde](/content/locations/morgenwelde.md)**: the capital.
- **[Aureluch](/content/locations/aureluch.md)**: the transport hub.
- **Third city**: not yet written.

## History

Quinten Hearspar always wanted to be a scholar. Defeat crept into his becoming, his most familiar feeling. He found himself toiling in the fields, just like his father before him. His blood, sweat and body being given to the ground, for an owner who never even showed his face at their plot, but would still demand ever-increasing payments.

Quinten's luck wouldn't end there, after a bandit-raid led to his mother being left immobile and brain damaged. Five months later, his father abandoned them, going on to raise a family with another woman. A year after that, he stopped supporting them financially, while mother and son burned through their collective savings to rehabilitate her.

One hot day, Quinten suffered a stroke whilst working in the field. His body spasmed, falling to the ground, choking on his own spit. His fractured mind glimpsed something no other mortal had. A world of pure order, of complete logic, lacking in all the wrongs this world had shown him.

He awoke days later in that field, his body deemed unworthy of a coffin. Quinten could never see the world in the same way again. Lines of logic, as clear as words on parchment, began appearing to him. He tried to tell those who asked about his recovery, but the stroke made his speech slurred, and when he was speaking coherently, the content of his speeches made very little sense. When he followed the logic, good things began to happen. He began making real money by implementing new irrigation techniques on his plot, which earned him a promotion. His mother was left alone, funds pulled when his new brain couldn't understand the familial bond.

Using his acquired funds, he left his farm. He travelled day and night, refusing to eat, drink or sleep, until he found an old quarry. The lines of logic showed him where to go: a golden nugget, in the middle of a large pile of rocks, unseeable by the naked eye. Painfully, severing his vocal cords, he ate the ore.

Like a man possessed, he dug. By the time his body gave out, he had collected another five of these ores, his body wrapped around them like a nursing mother. The first he sold, and using those funds, gathered a group of hearty workers to dig the area. With those profits, he secured the land itself. Then, he stopped selling. Creating blueprints and schemes he saw in his feverish dreams the first night he imbibed the ore, he made the first rudimentary steam engine. He used this for nothing other than drilling.

One day, the lines began to fade. It wasn't long after that when the losses began. In a desperate bid to see what he once did, he sank money into the last golden lines of order: into a machine to show him the logic of the world, to show him that clockwork universe. **Eye of Gold** was its name. By utilising its power, Quinten was able to transform his wealth into a settlement, then a town, then a city. Eventually it became the capital, [Morgenwelde](/content/locations/morgenwelde.md).

Technological advancements filled the city, and it became an industrial powerhouse, at the cost of those living there. The use of Morrow became widespread. Quinten found his body growing old, less useful. The logic told him to discard it. His body was found, mutilated and partially fused to the engine. The engine, if it ever worked, never will again.

## Foreign relations

### [Halingo](/content/locations/halingo.md)

Halingo and Ordon stand at a tense but neutral standoff. The rail network connecting the two countries was financed by both of them, a sign of co-operation, an outward truce. The truth of it is both countries are aware they both fill a niche: the Ordon ore and Ichor generate power. The leaders of Ordon are too self-centred and the Diesel Barons are too greedy to ever work together; both are aware only one can truly survive. Both vie for Shinkira's affection, a stalemate in the game they play. For now though, to the common folk, it appears as if both are in a truce.

### Skgurr

For several hundred years after the Oblate, the area now known as **Skgurr** was a violent, desolate wasteland, even if it did have inhabitants. The ancient order of the Ambit (political allies of Ordon) was primarily responsible for turning Skgurr into a habitable area. Locals were begrudgingly accepting. It was when Ordon believed it was entitled to the mysterious magical items that washed up along Skgurr's shoreline that things got heated.

A war machine was deployed to scare the locals and rescue the troops. When this machine began eroding due to the Acid Rain, a group of Steelbacks rescued the crew inside. This one act of heroism turned a simmering feud into a tentative alliance, the deployed platoon paying off their debt by joining the Steelbacks themselves, but not before returning to Ordon with some minor magical items as a delegacy. Knowing Skgurr's weather will forever hold off Ordon's war machines, the two countries became unlikely allies, with Ordon supplying basic goods in return for magical items.

### Shinkira

For hundreds of years, Shinkira was unassailable. Inhabited by [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md), it was believed no humans could live on that island. It was only when an Ordonian airship flew over the island patrolling for Armada that they realised the towering creatures that once defined the island were now gone. Instead, villages had sprung up. People were there all along.

Ordon attempted to deploy a delegacy as soon as possible, but news of this new country was leaked by an informant. The bureaucracy of Ordon had slowed it down, whilst other countries acted instinctively. In an act of cruelty, Halingo representatives reached the island on an oil-powered vessel and, knowing they had no chance of winning over the noble people, spent their time besmirching Ordon's name: not lying, but feeding them the worst stories of Ordon's sordid past. By the time the delegacy arrived, they were treated as hostile.

Instead, Shinkira decided to be independent, increasingly aware that if they were to ally firmly with any greater power, that power would instantly revolt against the other. Thus Shinkira remains politically neutral, but accepting of all, for the greater good. It is not known how long this neutrality will last.

### Nareth

Nareth and Ordon have a simple relationship. Nareth will back up Ordon when the time comes (the Nareth Truce); in return, Ordon will not interfere in Nareth affairs, and supplies them with 23 children each calendar year.

### Bratislor

It is safe to assume that without the Barrier, the two would be at violent war with one another. But, given the choice, Bratislor would be at war with everyone. The great Barrier divides the two countries, and ensures Bratislor is contained. That isn't to say the Barrier is impenetrable, far from it. Scholars and architects from both Ordon and Hjarthland worked in tandem to construct this Barrier, but it is Ordon that powers it and keeps it from functioning.

It is unclear whether it is the lack of power or a deliberate, sinister implication that the further north you travel, the weaker the Barrier becomes. It isn't unheard of for the occasional monstrosity, vaguely recognisable as human, to pass through. Most are destroyed instantly.

There have been no attempts from inside the Barrier to communicate formally.

### Armada

No real relationship exists between these two. Trusting reports from Skgurr, if Armada were ever to get close to the shoreline, it would be met with hostility.

### Hjarthland

Not yet written.

## GM notes

- Region names (Heartlands, Northern/Eastern/Western Ordon, Lowlands) are placeholders: "Replace these directional names once Ordon's internal regions have proper names." Eastern Ordon's transport city is unnamed ("Name Here").
- v3 note on attitude to Axius: "Tolerated. Something about the immortal."
- Bratislor: "Idea: fictional files based around these events."
- The wiki page still has unwritten sections: government detail, law and order, trade, wealth and class, airships, railways, society and culture, military, organisations, contact with other regions, recent history, notable people, and productivity-drug details (legal status, makers, users, effects, dependency).
- v4/V5 notes are checklists only: "1-paragraph summary of Ordon; main themes; current status; links to Morgwen, Government, Axius, Factions, D&D notes; a short 'what still needs doing' checklist."

name: The Far Realm
summary: The Neutral Evil outer plane of dissolution, home of Cthulhu, the Woodland Man. The Oblate awoke him, and the plane now seeps into the material world.
body:
**Plane god:** Cthulhu (also called the Woodland Man, and the Librarian)

**Plane god's motivation:** Dissolution. It despises anything tangible: form, thought, memory or consciousness. It desires nothing. The Oblate showed Cthulhu light, and awoke Him.

## Key features

- **Wrecks of Sanity.** The Far Realm is mostly featureless, but every now and then there are things the Great Old One has dreamed of: a shell of a dead god's thoughts, the petrified memory of a forgotten city, a continent of a mortal's failed dream.
- **Aberrations.** Tumours of thought.
- **Abyssal Strain.** When the Oblate receded, it didn't leave the material plane unscathed. Like greased paper, reality seeps through, just as the Far Realm seeps back. Seeping Maw cultists on the other side are desperate to pierce reality.

## Effect on players

Creatures of the Far Realm may have these traits:

- **Entropy of the Abyss.** Whenever the creature deals bludgeoning, piercing or slashing damage, it can change the damage type to necrotic.
- **Poison Tolerant.** The creature has advantage on saving throws it makes to avoid or end the poisoned condition on itself.
- **Siege Monster.** The creature deals double damage to objects and structures.

## GM notes

- The v3 note calls this plane "the Abyss" in several places, and two traits keep that wording. The user confirmed (2026-11-04) that the text describes the Far Realm. The Abyss is a separate Chaotic Evil plane.
- The Seeping Maw is a Cthulhu cult (v3, Random Characters and Hooks). It isn't curated yet.

name: Creatures of Kurovia
summary: Index of Kurovia's creatures by region, rarity and Challenge Rating, with the setting's rarity and CR scales.
body:
The creatures of Kurovia have been shaped by their environments, regional manifestations of Axius and the cultures that live alongside them. They can be browsed by location, rarity or Challenge Rating.

The [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md) (the Hundred Gods) are catalogued separately.

## By region

Creatures are listed according to the region in which they are most commonly found. Migratory or widespread creatures may appear under more than one region.

| Region | Environment | Creatures |
|----|----|----|
| **[Ordon](/content/locations/ordon.md)** | Industrial cities, farmland, mines and older rural wilderness | [Cragback](/content/creatures/cragback.md), [Driftling](/content/creatures/driftling.md), [Shellbill](/content/creatures/shellbill.md) |
| **[Halingo](/content/locations/halingo.md)** | Deserts, rocky wastes, Ichor fields and railway settlements | [Dustkip](/content/creatures/dustkip.md), [Sunsnare](/content/creatures/sunsnare.md) |
| **Skgurr** | Storm coasts, Morov rivers, dark highlands and sea caves | [Shellbill](/content/creatures/shellbill.md) |
| **Shinkira** | Forests, mountains, cities and Utsuro-altered ecosystems | [Driftling](/content/creatures/driftling.md), [Shellbill](/content/creatures/shellbill.md) |
| **Bratislor** | Haze-contaminated wilderness, ruins and containment zones | — |
| **Hjarthland** | Frozen forests, glaciers, mountains and permanent winter | [Cragback](/content/creatures/cragback.md), [Driftling](/content/creatures/driftling.md) |
| **Nareth** | Rainforests, swamps, rivers and rapidly growing ecosystems | [Driftling](/content/creatures/driftling.md), [Lanthart](/content/creatures/lanthart.md), [Shellbill](/content/creatures/shellbill.md) |
| **Targoth** | High mountains, abandoned settlements and isolated valleys | [Kharuun](/content/creatures/kharuun.md) |
| **Armada** | Ships, docks, floating districts and the surrounding seas | [Knelhen](/content/creatures/knelhen.md) |

### Widespread creatures

**Widespread creatures** are found across several regions of Kurovia rather than being associated with a single country: [Cragback](/content/creatures/cragback.md), [Driftling](/content/creatures/driftling.md), [Ritual Husk](/content/creatures/ritual-husk.md), [Shellbill](/content/creatures/shellbill.md).

## By rarity

Rarity describes how frequently a creature is encountered in the world. It does not necessarily indicate how dangerous it is. A creature may be common in one region while remaining almost unknown elsewhere; each creature uses the rarity that best represents its status within its principal habitat.

| Rarity | Definition | Creatures |
|----|----|----|
| **Common** | Frequently encountered within its natural habitat. Usually familiar to local inhabitants. | [Driftling](/content/creatures/driftling.md), [Dustkip](/content/creatures/dustkip.md), [Shellbill](/content/creatures/shellbill.md) |
| **Uncommon** | Known to local communities but not encountered regularly. | [Cragback](/content/creatures/cragback.md), [Lanthart](/content/creatures/lanthart.md), [Sunsnare](/content/creatures/sunsnare.md) |
| **Rare** | Seldom encountered and usually limited to particular environments or circumstances. | [Kharuun](/content/creatures/kharuun.md), [Mournback](/content/creatures/mournback.md) |
| **Very Rare** | Known from only a small number of sightings, territories or surviving populations. | [Knelhen](/content/creatures/knelhen.md), [Ritual Husk](/content/creatures/ritual-husk.md) |
| **Legendary** | Famous creatures whose existence may shape local history, religion or folklore. | — |
| **Unique** | A single known individual, species-ending survivor or creature without confirmed equivalents. | — |

## By Challenge Rating

Challenge Rating (CR) represents the approximate threat a creature poses in combat.

| CR range | General threat | Creatures |
|----|----|----|
| **CR 0** | Normally harmless, although it may still possess unusual abilities. | [Dustkip](/content/creatures/dustkip.md) |
| **CR 1/8–1/2** | A threat to an untrained individual or poorly prepared traveller. | [Driftling](/content/creatures/driftling.md), [Lanthart](/content/creatures/lanthart.md) |
| **CR 1–4** | A local threat suitable for lower-level adventurers. | [Cragback](/content/creatures/cragback.md), [Sunsnare](/content/creatures/sunsnare.md) |
| **CR 5–10** | A serious regional danger capable of threatening settlements or trained forces. | [Kharuun](/content/creatures/kharuun.md), [Knelhen](/content/creatures/knelhen.md), [Ritual Husk](/content/creatures/ritual-husk.md) |
| **CR 11–16** | A major threat requiring experienced adventurers or organised military action. | [Mournback](/content/creatures/mournback.md) |
| **CR 17–20** | An exceptional threat capable of devastating cities or influencing entire regions. | — |
| **CR 21+** | A world-level threat possessing extraordinary or near-mythic power. | — |
| **Unrated** | A creature without completed combat statistics or one not intended for combat. | [Shellbill](/content/creatures/shellbill.md) |

## By creature type

- **Aberration**: [Kharuun](/content/creatures/kharuun.md), [Ritual Husk](/content/creatures/ritual-husk.md)
- **Abomination**: [Mournback](/content/creatures/mournback.md)
- **Beast**: [Cragback](/content/creatures/cragback.md), [Driftling](/content/creatures/driftling.md), [Dustkip](/content/creatures/dustkip.md), [Lanthart](/content/creatures/lanthart.md)
- **Monstrosity**: [Knelhen](/content/creatures/knelhen.md), [Sunsnare](/content/creatures/sunsnare.md)

## GM notes

- The wiki's index also lists the categories Constructs, Dragons, Elementals, Fey, Giants, Humanoids, Oozes, Plants and Undead (all empty so far), plus "Sea creatures" and "Domesticated creatures" groupings. Its habitat categories (urban, farmland, forest, mountain, desert, swamp, coastal, sea, subterranean) are empty too.
- Wiki note: "To update: Hundred Gods".
- The Shellbill has no Challenge Rating yet, and the Mournback has no region.

## Tiers

Gods are ranked by how widely they are worshipped:

- **Major:** celebrated everywhere; everyone knows of them. The equivalent of the great real-world religions.
- **Minor:** niche faiths with a narrower following.
- **Cult:** gods almost no one knows about, worshipped in only one or two places across the world.

**Old Gods.** Sometime after creation, the Old Gods struck the pact that made [Carceri](/content/locations/carceri.md). [Kelemvor](/content/deities/kelemvor.md) is an Old God. Which other gods count as Old Gods isn't recorded yet.

name: Timeline
body:
# The Dawn
Summary:  Supposedly, two brothers, Ornn and Bruen, entered the void. The infinite nothing. Their interaction disturbed the great silence. The darkness that had been sleeping forever awoke. The three interacted, protecting themselves from each others accidental harm. Their interplay brought forth Pia, a young woman of immense beauty and strength.

The darkness retreated, believing it had lost, Pia seemed like everything it wasn't - strong, overt and good. But it remained watching. Whilst Pia seemed incorruptible, the two brothers had a rift between them.

Ornn believed Pia should be groomed as a hero, the new champion of to pioneer a new way of life, a shining beacon of the glory of chaos. Bruen believed that life should be so precious just to exist, and to follow the current order, the way things were; being sheltered and living out their life comfortably with no stress. Darkness saw this division and acted, speaking in each brothers ear.

The two began arguing, then fighting. Pia stepped between them, only to accidentally be punched, breaking her jaw. The two looked in horror in what they had done, each blaming the other - a once perfect vision of beauty corrupted. Ironically, seeing Pia's now flawed features, it was the first time darkness ever felt an emotion. Pia's once perfect features, sheer strength was undermined by the folly of others. Darkness realised it could still act with Pia around. It realised it cared for Pia - despite them being polar opposites, there was this implicit understanding between them. A silent acknowledgement of respect. It realised it cared for Pia. It attempted to undo what it had started, but alas the brothers was so twisted against the other, so bitter. Each drew their sword and each drew blood. Both ended up slain by the other.

Pia remained there, watching the bodies of her creators in the infinite void. She reached out, and began to create something new. She invited darkness to join her, to make something of this. She wanted to create a place where they could live in harmony, one family. Equal amounts of each. Taking the blood and remains of the brothers, Pia accepted darkness. All that remained was her ever beating heart. The four of them created Kuroiva.

And yet, Pia remained. It was a curious sensation, to have ceased existing in one reality, but exist in another. So when Pia was brought into existence again, by the two brothers. She smiled. She got to go round again. Each time, it happened differently. Sometimes, Ornn and Pia were the only survivors - creating a different world, a different Plane from their outcome. Sometimes it would be darkness and Ornn. Then, just Pia. Around and around they went. 9 different planes exist, will exist, have existed. Each one made up of the different denizens of the void. But, Pia thought, none were as perfect as Kurovia.

Each outcome created it's own Plane of existence, each a mirror of another, and yet somehow all linked.

Each plane births it's first creation into being, a personification of it's existence. These are listed here:

- Lawful Good - Mount Celestia
-  Neutral Good - Elysium
-  Chaotic Good - Aracadia
-  Lawful Neutral - Mechanus
-  True Neutral - Kurovia
- Chaotic Neutral - Limbo
- Lawful Evil - Avernus
- Neutral Evil - The Far Realm
- Chaotic Evil - Abyss

# The First Era (1E)
For the point of keeping this short(er), the history will only focus on Kurovia.

# The Second Era (2E)
The Oblate had obliterated Kurovia, but the Planar overlap has allowed the junctions and rules of reality to break down further. The world was unstable. Only a few years after, the Sorcerer-King Seneth would rise to power, as seen in The Serpent's Price

- Hunting Grounds
- Merchantile

name: Umbuso Hazard Index
summary: The UMB Research Directorate's six-factor (S/L/A/C/P/K) hazard score for Umbuso, averaged into a 1.00-5.00 UHI and a grade from I (Existential) to V (Limited).
body:
Standardised Assessment of Umbuso Threat

**Designation:** UHI\
**Current Revision:** IV\
**Status:** ACTIVE STANDARD\
**Authorising Body:** ████████████████

**RESEARCH NOTE**

The UHI measures the **hazard presented by an Umbuso**, not its physical strength.

A low score indicates greater danger.

**1 is the worst possible rating. 5 is the best.**

## Method

Every confirmed [Umbuso](/content/lore/umbuso.md) is assessed across six factors:

| Code  | Factor             | Measures                                         |
|-------|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| **S** | **Scale**          | Maximum credible population or area affected.    |
| **L** | **Lethality**      | Expected severity of direct exposure.            |
| **A** | **Activation**     | Likelihood of hostile or hazardous behaviour.    |
| **C** | **Containability** | Humanity's ability to restrict or neutralise it. |
| **P** | **Predictability** | Ability to anticipate or avoid an encounter.     |
| **K** | **Knowledge**      | Reliability of current scientific understanding. |

**UHI = (S + L + A + C + P + K) ÷ 6**

Decimal scores are retained in all formal documentation.

## Assessment Scale

| Score | Scale | Lethality | Activation | Containment | Predictability | Knowledge |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| **1** | World | Terminal | Inherent | Uncontainable | Unavoidable | Incomprehensible |
| **2** | Continental | Extreme | Aggressive | Unmanageable | Unpredictable | Poorly understood |
| **3** | Regional | Severe | Reactive | Restrictable | Detectable | Partially understood |
| **4** | Local | Moderate | Passive | Manageable | Predictable | Well documented |
| **5** | Individual | Low | Dormant | Controllable | Avoidable | Understood |

**Scale does not measure physical size.**

An Umbuso capable of appearing worldwide but threatening only isolated individuals would not automatically receive **S1**.

## Hazard Grades

The calculated UHI determines the entity's formal hazard grade.

| UHI           | Grade   | Classification |
|---------------|---------|----------------|
| **1.00–1.49** | **I**   | EXISTENTIAL    |
| **1.50–2.49** | **II**  | Catastrophic   |
| **2.50–3.49** | **III** | Severe         |
| **3.50–4.49** | **IV**  | Hazardous      |
| **4.50–5.00** | **V**   | Limited        |

A full research designation is written as:

**UMB-028 KHARVASSA**\
**UHI 2.00-II**\
S2 / L1 / A3 / C1 / P3 / K2

## Current Assessments

| Archive | Entity          | S     | L     | A     | C     | P     | K     | UHI      | Grade |

| UMB-017 | [Hoshikui](/content/creatures/hoshikui.md)    | 3     | 2     | 3     | 2     | 3     | 2     | **2.50** | III   |
| UMB-028 | [Kharvassa](/content/creatures/kharvassa.md)   | 2     | 1     | 3     | 1     | 3     | 2     | **2.00** | II    |
| UMB-033 | [Ulveth](/content/creatures/ulveth.md) | 4 | 3 | 1 | 5 | 5 | 4 | **3.67** | IV |
| UMB-034 | [Saqramallki](/content/creatures/saqramallki.md) | 4 | 3 | 2 | 3 | 3 | 5 | **3.33** | III |
| UMB-041 | [Oruvath](/content/creatures/oruvath.md)     | 3     | 2     | 3     | 2     | 4     | 2     | **2.67** | III   |
| UMB-052 | [Elyrra](/content/creatures/elyrra.md) | 4 | 5 | 3 | 1 | 2 | 4 | **3.17** | III |
| UMB-063 | [Vaelkr](/content/creatures/vaelkr.md)      | 3     | 2     | 3     | 2     | 4     | 3     | **2.83** | III   |
| UMB-076 | [Tathis](/content/creatures/tathis.md) | 5 | 2 | 1 | 5 | 5 | 5 | **3.83** | IV |

## Revision Policy

UHI ratings are **not permanent**.

New behaviour, casualties or research may immediately alter an assessment.

**RECLASSIFICATION EXAMPLE**

CURRENT: UHI 1.83-II

REASON:

A reduction of more than **0.50** following a single incident requires mandatory review of all existing containment and evacuation doctrine.

name: Umbuso
summary: The Umbuso, traditionally the Hundred Gods, are an irregular class of extremely rare, ancient and destructive entities catalogued by the UMB Research Directorate.
body:
**ARCHIVE:** UMB-000\
**CLASSIFICATION:** EXTREME BIOLOGICAL ANOMALIES\
**CATALOGUE RANGE:** UMB-001 — UMB-100\
**CONFIRMED ENTRIES:** ████\
**PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE ENTRIES:** 6\
**ACCESS:** PARTIAL

**ARCHIVAL NOTICE**

**Umbuso** and **the Hundred Gods** describe the same class of entity.

*Umbuso* is the modern scholarly term.

*Hundred Gods* is the traditional Shinkiran designation.

The name is not evidence that exactly one hundred entities exist.

Catalogue numbers between **UMB-001** and **UMB-100** are administrative identifiers only.

Missing numbers should not be interpreted as unused.

“They called them gods because nothing smaller could explain them.”

— Author unknown

## Classification

The **Umbuso** are an irregular group of extremely rare creatures documented throughout the oldest surviving records of Kurovia.

They are not believed to form a single species.

No shared anatomy, ancestry, habitat or reproductive system has been established.

Classification instead reflects a recurring collection of characteristics:

- extreme biological abnormality;
- extraordinary longevity or historical continuity;
- unusually high destructive potential;
- resistance to conventional intervention;
- and behaviour which cannot be adequately explained by existing natural sciences.

Most people will never encounter an Umbuso.

This is considered desirable.

## The Hundred Gods

The oldest substantial records originate in Shinkira, where such entities were collectively referred to as the **Hundred Gods**.

The translation is imperfect.

Some were worshipped.

Others were avoided.

Several appear to have inspired buildings, roads, rituals and entire settlements designed around the simple objective of never attracting their attention.

**RECOVERED SHINKIRAN INSCRIPTION**

*Do not ask whether it is beast or god.*

*Ask whether it has noticed you.*

## Hazard Assessment

Confirmed Umbuso receive an **[UHI](/content/lore/umbuso-hazard-index.md)** assessment.

Six factors are rated from **1 to 5**:

**S** — Scale\
**L** — Lethality\
**A** — Activation\
**C** — Containability\
**P** — Predictability\
**K** — Knowledge

**1 represents maximum hazard.**

**5 represents minimum hazard.**

The six values are averaged to produce the final UHI.

**EXAMPLE**

UMB-017 // HOSHIKUI

UHI **2.50-III**

S3 / L2 / A3 / C2 / P3 / K2

See: **[Umbuso Hazard Index](/content/lore/umbuso-hazard-index.md)**

name: The World Tree
summary: The cosmology of the world. Nine planes, each born from a different outcome of the creation at the Dawn, each tied to an alignment and personified by its first creation, its plane god.
body:
## Origin

At the Dawn, Pia, born from the meeting of the brothers Ornn and Bruen with the darkness of the void, made Kurovia with the darkness from the brothers' remains. Pia then found herself brought into existence again, and again, and each time the story went differently. Sometimes only Ornn and Pia survived; sometimes only the darkness and Ornn; sometimes only Pia. Each outcome created its own plane of existence, each a mirror of another, and yet all somehow linked. Nine planes exist, will exist, have existed. But, Pia thought, none were as perfect as Kurovia.

Each plane births its first creation into being: a personification of its existence, its **plane god**.

The full creation myth is in [The Timeline](/content/lore/timeline.md) (The Dawn).

## The nine planes

| Alignment | Plane | Plane god | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lawful Good | Mount Celestia | The Triad | Plane god's motivation: preservation. |
| Neutral Good | Elysium | — | The v3 note contains only the word "Lathander". |
| Chaotic Good | Arcadia | — | |
| Lawful Neutral | [Mechanus](/content/locations/mechanus.md) | [Primus](/content/deities/primus.md) | Perfection. One of the only planes a mortal has contacted directly. |
| True Neutral | Kurovia | — | The material world. |
| Chaotic Neutral | [Limbo](/content/locations/limbo.md) | — | Raw, untamed creative chaos. Contains [Carceri](/content/locations/carceri.md), the first demi-plane. |
| Lawful Evil | Avernus | — | |
| Neutral Evil | [The Far Realm](/content/locations/the-far-realm.md) | Cthulhu (the Woodland Man, the Librarian) | Dissolution. Awoken by the Oblate. |
| Chaotic Evil | Abyss | — | |

## Structure

The v3 vault arranges the World Tree into **Outer Planes** (the nine above, apart from Kurovia), **Inner Planes** (the Underdark) and **Astral Space**. The Underdark and Astral Space are named but not yet described.

## The planes after the Oblate

The Oblate obliterated Kurovia, and the planar overlap it caused let the junctions and rules of reality break down further. The world was left unstable. The Far Realm in particular now seeps through into the material plane.

## GM notes

- Ideas for sub-regions, listed in the Timeline: Pandemonium, 7 Deadly Sins, Hunting Grounds, Merchantile.
- v3 spells Arcadia "Aracadia". The Arcadia note contains only "test".

name: Haze (Contamination)
summary: Six-level contamination condition from exposure to the Haze or Delerium, with symptoms, random mutations, madness and monstrous transformation at level 6.
body:
*This entry covers Haze the **mechanic**. Haze is also the name of a regional variant of Axius.*

The world of Kurovia is one that has been broken before. Characters may be exposed to eldritch pollutants within the **Haze** or arcane radiation emitted by Delerium. These hazards cause a new condition called **contamination**, which inflicts both debilitating symptoms and otherworldly mutations.

Contamination is measured in six levels. An effect can give a creature one or more levels of contamination, as specified in the effect's description. If an already contaminated creature suffers another effect that causes further contamination, its current contamination level increases by the amount specified in the effect's description.

In addition, whenever a character finishes a long rest while they have one or more contamination levels, roll `1d20`. On a 1, they gain one contamination level.

Upon reaching contamination level 6 or higher, the creature transforms as described in the [Monstrous Transformation](#monstrous-transformation) section.

## Contamination Symptoms

A contaminated creature suffers the symptoms from its current level as well as all lower levels.

| Level | Symptoms                                              |
|-------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| 1     | None.                                                 |
| 2     | Hit points regained by expending Hit Dice are halved. |
| 3     | No hit points are regained at the end of a long rest. |
| 4     | Damage dealt by weapon attacks and spells is halved.  |
| 5     | Incapacitated.           |
| 6     | Monstrous Transformation.                             |

## Mutations

In addition to suffering symptoms, whenever a character gains a contamination level, they roll `1d6`. If the result is equal to or lower than the character's current contamination level, the creature gains a mutation.

The Game Master may choose the mutation or determine it randomly by rolling `1d20` on the Mutations table. If the result is the same as a mutation currently affecting the creature, the Game Master chooses a different mutation or rolls again.

| 1d20 | Mutation |
|----|----|
| 1 | **Rampant Mutation.** Roll twice, ignoring this result on subsequent rolls. |
| 2 | **Rasping.** Your vocal cords warp, and you may only speak in a halting gurgle. If you have 4 or more contamination levels, your tongue rots and falls out, and you can no longer speak. |
| 3 | **Wasting.** Your fingernails, teeth and toenails start falling out. `2d6` fall out for each contamination level you have gained. |
| 4 | **Rotting.** Your lips, nose and ears blacken and wither. If you reach 4 or more contamination levels, they rot and fall off. You can still speak and hear. |
| 5 | **Molting.** Painful blisters, welts and multicoloured lesions appear across your skin. They burst and peel away painfully, exposing the raw sinew underneath. Once you reach 4 contamination levels, your skin entirely sloughs off. |
| 6 | **Shedding.** Whenever you gain a contamination level, some of your hair falls out in patches. Once you reach 4 or more contamination levels, all hair on your body completely falls out. |
| 7 | **Lambent Glow.** You emit dim octarine light to a range of 10 feet. If you have 4 or more contamination levels, you instead emit bright light to a range of 30 feet. |
| 8 | **Ocular Tumours.** An eyeball opens somewhere on your body for each contamination level you have gained. If you have 4 or more contamination levels, you can see in all directions. |
| 9 | **Spiked Growths.** At the start of each of your turns, you deal 5 (`1d10`) piercing damage to any creature you are grappling. |
| 10 | **Aquatic Adaptation.** You sprout fish-like fins and gills. You gain a swimming speed equal to your land speed and can breathe underwater. If you have 4 or more contamination levels, you can only breathe underwater, but can hold your breath outside water for up to 1 hour. |
| 11 | **Amorphous Form.** Your bones and organs become gelatinous. You can move through a space as narrow as 6 inches wide without squeezing. |
| 12 | **Chitinous Skin.** Shell-like growths appear across your body, giving you a +1 bonus to AC. If you have 4 or more contamination levels, this bonus increases to +2. |
| 13 | **Cyclopean Vision.** Your eyes merge into a single central eye which can emit an energy beam as a ranged spell attack using your Intelligence modifier for the attack roll. On a hit, it deals `2d6` radiant damage. |
| 14 | **Spatial Displacement.** You can cast misty step once for each contamination level you have gained. You regain these uses when you finish a long rest. |
| 15 | **Tentacled Limb.** One of your arms becomes a fleshy tentacle. When you make a melee attack on your turn, increase your reach by 5 feet. |
| 16 | **Spider Climb.** You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed. You can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check. |
| 17 | **Whispering Voices.** You gain telepathy to a range of 10 feet, but other people hear it as their own voice. If you have 4 or more contamination levels, the range extends to 60 feet. |
| 18 | **Belly Maw.** A toothy mouth appears on your stomach, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. On a hit, it deals piercing damage equal to `1d6` + your Strength modifier. |
| 19 | **Eyeless Sight.** Your eyes become milky orbs, and you gain blindsight to a range of 10 feet. If you have 4 or more contamination levels, your eyes rot out and dim octarine light burns within the sockets. Your blindsight increases to 30 feet, but you are blind beyond this radius. |
| 20 | **Arcane Blood.** You gain an additional spell slot of the highest level you can cast, to a maximum of 5th level. If you do not have spell slots, your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to your level. This benefit is doubled while you have 4 or more contamination levels. |

## Removing Contamination

Only specific magic can remove contamination levels. Creatures do not recover naturally.

The purge contamination spell can remove contamination, but leaves affected characters exhausted. A heal spell removes all contamination levels and mutations from a contaminated character.

An effect which removes a contamination level also removes one randomly determined mutation. All contamination symptoms end and all mutations are removed if a creature's contamination level is reduced below 1.

Skin, hair, fingernails and toenails lost to mutations regrow normally once contamination is removed. However, a regenerate spell or similar magic is required to restore other body parts, such as teeth, limbs or eyes.

Appendages or limbs which developed as a result of mutations wither and fall off when contamination is removed. Other warped body parts return to their original form.

## Death and Dying While Contaminated

When a humanoid creature with any contamination levels dies, it animates as a Haze Husk 24 hours later.

A creature with six or more class levels or Hit Dice rises as a Haze Wight instead.

Being raised from the dead reduces a creature's contamination level by one.

## Monstrous Transformation

A creature who reaches contamination level 6 or higher begins transforming into a horrific monster controlled by the Game Master.

Once triggered, the transformation finishes in 1 round and is thereafter permanent. Game Masters are encouraged to narrate a suitably gory description of the transformation.

The Game Master chooses the creature's new form, which is most often an aberration or monstrosity such as a Delerium Dreg, Haze Hulk or Gibbering Mouther.

The new form usually has a challenge rating similar to that of the original creature, but under appropriate circumstances the Game Master may choose one that is much higher or lower.

The creature's game statistics are entirely replaced by those of the chosen monster. The creature assumes the new form's hit points and Hit Dice.

All contamination levels are removed, though the Game Master may grant the new form additional traits similar to any beneficial mutations the creature previously possessed.

The Game Master determines what remains of the original creature's personality and memories, if anything. Regardless, the creature is invariably driven mad by the transformation and falls under the Game Master's control.

### Reversing the Transformation

The means of reversing a monstrous transformation are completely unknown at the outset of the campaign.

A monstrous transformation is widely regarded as permanent, though many still search the ruins for answers. Those who do may eventually be able to research the siphon contamination spell.

A wish spell or similar magic can restore a single transformed creature to its previous form, removing all madness and contamination in the process.

This is considered a stressful use of the *wish* spell. There is therefore a 33 percent chance that the caster will be unable to cast *wish* ever again after using the spell in this manner.

The transformation is otherwise irreversible by any means short of divine intervention.

At the Game Master's discretion, it may be possible to temporarily alleviate a transformed creature's innate madness. However, an intelligent monster receiving long-term treatment may eventually conspire to contaminate or subtly corrupt its caretakers.

## Madness

| 1d10 | Madness |
|----|----|
| 1 | “I wish I didn't have all these useless organs inside me.” |
| 2 | “The contamination is a blessing which will transform me into a wondrous creature.” |
| 3 | “The monsters are civilians trying to live a peaceful life! We need to protect them!” |
| 4 | “I must wear a flesh-coat made from my slain enemies to gain their strength!” |
| 5 | “My companions died in the ruins. I'm sorry, friends. You are merely ghosts haunting me. You aren't real. Stop trying to talk to other people.” |
| 6 | “I need to eat everything I can find. It's probably going to be my last meal.” |
| 7 | “The ruins are so beautiful at night. I could spend forever wandering the streets by moonlight. We should go tonight! Let's go every night!” |
| 8 | “Don't you fools get it? If you die in the ruins, you die in real life!” |
| 9 | “A sinister cabal of disembodied hands is plotting against me.” |
| 10 | “I must go into the ruins and kill. Rip and tear, until it is done.” |

name: Lingering Injuries
summary: d20 lingering-injury tables by damage type, rolled when a creature drops to 0 hit points or fails a save by 5 or more.
body:
A creature might sustain a lingering injury under the following circumstances:

- When it drops to 0 hit points
- When it fails a saving throw by 5 points or more

The type of injury sustained is determined by the damage type that caused it.

## Acid

| d20 | Injury | Description | Length |
|----|----|----|----|
| 1 | **Blindness** | Your eyes are destroyed; you gain the blinded condition. Magic such as the regenerate spell can restore your sight. | — |
| 2 | **Partial Blindness** | Your eyes are damaged. You have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and cannot see more than 30 feet ahead of you. | — |
| 3 | **Destroyed Hand** | You lose a hand or arm. You can no longer hold anything with two hands, and you can hold only a single object at a time. | — |
| 4 | **Destroyed Leg** | Your speed on foot is halved, and you must use a crutch or cane to move. You fall prone after using the Dash action. You have disadvantage on Dexterity checks made to balance. | — |
| 5–7 | **Destroyed Inventory** | Your armour and backpack become useless. You lose all but `1d4` of your rations, as well as `1d12` other items. | — |
| 8–10 | **Destroyed Weapon** | Your weapons are destroyed. | — |
| 11–13 | **Horrible Disfigurement** | You suffer acid burns so extensive that the scars cannot be easily concealed. You have disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks and advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks. | — |
| 14–16 | **Blisters** | You have severe blisters and disadvantage on Dexterity checks. The blisters heal if you receive magical healing. Alternatively, someone can tend to them and make a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check once every 24 hours. After seven successes, the blisters heal. | `1d4` weeks |
| 17–20 | **Minor Disfigurement** | You have acid-burn scars, but they have no adverse effect. | — |

## Bludgeoning or Force

| d20 | Injury | Description | Length |
|----|----|----|----|
| 1 | **Coma** | You fall unconscious and cannot be woken by healing. You awaken after one hour. | 1 hour |
| 2 | **Broken Leg** | Your speed on foot is halved, and you must use a cane or crutch to move. You fall prone after using the Dash action and have disadvantage on Dexterity checks made to balance. If your leg is splinted with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check, it heals twice as fast. | `1d6` weeks |
| 3 | **Destroyed Hand** | You lose the use of a hand or arm. You can no longer hold anything with two hands, and you can hold only a single object at a time. If your arm is splinted with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check, it heals twice as fast. | `1d6` weeks |
| 4–6 | **Punctured Lung** | You can take either an action or a bonus action on your turn, but not both. If both lungs are punctured, your hit points drop to 0 and you immediately begin dying. | `1d4` weeks |
| 7–9 | **Tinnitus** | Your ears ring following the blow. You have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing. | `1d10` weeks |
| 10–12 | **Concussion** | You have disadvantage on Intelligence checks and saving throws. The concussion heals if you receive any magical healing. | 2 weeks |
| 13–15 | **Severe Bruising** | You suffer severe bruising over an extensive portion of your body. Whenever you take bludgeoning or force damage, you take an additional `1d8` bludgeoning damage. | `1d4` weeks |
| 16–20 | **Broken Nose** | You have a broken nose. Any magical healing mends it, although it may heal crooked if it is crooked when the healing is applied. | `1d4` days |

## Cold

| d20 | Injury | Description | Length |
|----|----|----|----|
| 1–2 | **Gangrene** | Gangrene spreads across one of your hands. Removing the hand within 24 hours limits the infection to the hand. Waiting longer allows the gangrene to spread to other areas. | — |
| 3 | **Anosmia** | You lose your sense of smell and taste. You automatically fail ability checks that rely on smell or taste. | — |
| 4 | **Neuralgia** | You cannot take reactions. If you take both an action and bonus action on your turn, you must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw to perform the second action. | — |
| 5–7 | **System Shock** | You cannot seem to become warm. Each night, make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, you gain one level of exhaustion. | `1d4` days |
| 8–10 | **Cold Hearted** | Each day, regardless of your condition, roll for exhaustion. Exhaustion gained in this way cannot exceed one level. | `1d4` weeks |
| 11–13 | **Frozen Extremity** | One of your extremities becomes numb. You have disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws. | 3 weeks |
| 14–16 | **Whooping Cough** | You suffer from a harsh and persistent cough. You have disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. | 2 weeks |
| 17–20 | **Anosmia** | You lose your sense of smell and taste. You automatically fail ability checks that rely on smell or taste. | — |

## Fire and Lightning

Fire injuries are characterised by their stacking effects. Repeatedly falling to fire damage causes increasingly severe burns.

| d20 | Injury | Description | Length |
|----|----|----|----|
| 1 | **Neuralgia** | Whenever you attempt to take an action in combat, you must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, you lose the action. | `1d6` weeks |
| 2 | **Fourth-Degree Burns** | You have disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity and Constitution checks and saving throws. If you fail a saving throw against an effect that causes fire damage, you are also stunned until the end of your next turn. | — |
| 3 | **Third-Degree Burns** | You have disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity and Constitution checks, as well as Constitution saving throws. If you fail a saving throw against an effect that causes fire damage, you are also stunned until the end of your next turn. Someone can tend to the burns and make a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check once each week. After ten successes, the burns heal. If you already have third-degree burns, you instead suffer fourth-degree burns. Taking more than 15 points of fire damage in a single turn also upgrades the injury to fourth-degree burns. | — |
| 4 | **Second-Degree Burns** | You have disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity and Constitution checks. If you already have second-degree burns, you instead suffer third-degree burns. Taking more than 10 points of fire damage in a single turn also upgrades the injury to third-degree burns. | 1 week |
| 5–7 | **Internal Injuries** | You lose a number of Hit Dice equal to `1d4 + half your level` while injured. | `1d4` weeks |
| 8–10 | **Cardiac Injury** | You gain one level of exhaustion that cannot be removed normally. Whenever you fail a saving throw against fear or a fear effect, you gain another level of exhaustion, which can be removed normally. Magic such as the *regenerate* spell can heal the cardiac damage. | `1d4` weeks |
| 11–13 | **Horrible Disfigurement** | You have burn scars so extensive that they cannot be easily concealed. You have disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks and advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks. | 2 weeks |
| 14–16 | **Blisters** | You have severe blisters and disadvantage on Dexterity checks. Once each week, someone can tend to the blisters with a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check and create a paste. Applying the paste temporarily suppresses the effect, but does not heal it. | `1d4` weeks |
| 17–20 | **First-Degree Burns** | You have superficial but painful burns. Whenever you take fire damage, you take an additional `1d4` fire damage. If you already have first-degree burns, you instead suffer second-degree burns. Taking more than 5 points of fire damage in a single turn also upgrades the injury to second-degree burns. | `1d8` weeks |

## Necrotic

Necrotic injuries tend to have longer-lasting and debilitating effects, further hindering characters without divine intervention.

| d20 | Injury | Description | Length |
|----|----|----|----|
| 1 | **Full Decay** | Your body is fundamentally damaged. Your hit point maximum is reduced by 1 every 24 hours. For every week that passes, a new body part falls off. Holy intervention is required. | 10 weeks |
| 2 | **Incubator** | You become an incubator for a new plague. | `1d6` weeks |
| 3 | **Dark Spirit** | You believe that you can see a demon inside you. It may appear to you. | — |
| 4 | **Necrotic Discharge** | Everything you touch, including allies and objects, takes `1d6` necrotic damage. | `1d4` weeks |
| 5–7 | **Insanity** | Roll on the Long-Term Madness table. | — |
| 8–10 | **Undead Stench** | You smell like rotting flesh. You have disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks. Magical healing of 6th level or higher removes the smell. | `1d4` weeks |
| 11–13 | **Minor Decay** | Your hit point maximum is reduced by 1 every 24 hours while the wound persists. If your hit point maximum drops to 0, you die. The wound heals if you receive magical healing. | — |
| 14–16 | **Inflammation** | Your muscles are irritated and inflamed. You have disadvantage on Strength checks. | 2 weeks |
| 17–20 | **Necrotic Discolouration** | White and grey spots appear on your cheeks. The spots have no adverse effect. Magical healing of 6th level or higher removes them. | — |

## Piercing and Slashing

Piercing and slashing damage are relatively common, so their lingering injuries are generally less severe.

| d20 | Injury | Description | Length |
|----|----|----|----|
| 1 | **Lose an Eye** | You have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight and on ranged attack rolls. Magic such as the *regenerate* spell can restore the lost eye. If you have no eyes remaining after sustaining this injury, you are blinded. | — |
| 2 | **Throat Injury** | You gain one level of exhaustion that cannot be removed normally. You also have disadvantage on Constitution checks. Magic such as the *regenerate* spell can heal the injury. | — |
| 3 | **Groin Injury** | Your speed on foot is halved, and you must use a cane or crutch to move. You cannot take the Dash action and are sterile. Magic such as the *regenerate* spell can heal the injury. | — |
| 4 | **Cardiac Injury** | You gain one level of exhaustion that cannot be removed normally. Whenever you fail a saving throw against fear or a fear effect, you gain another level of exhaustion, which can be removed normally. You frequently find yourself short of breath. | `1d4` weeks |
| 5–7 | **Pierced Stomach** | When you complete a long rest, you must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain the poisoned condition until you complete another long rest. Magical healing of 6th level or higher, such as heal or *regenerate*, heals the pierced stomach. It also heals naturally if you spend ten days doing nothing but resting. | 10 days |
| 8–10 | **Infested Wound** | Dirt, grime or poison enters the wound. You take `1d10` poison damage every day until it is cured. | — |
| 11–14 | **Horrible Scar** | You are disfigured to the extent that the wound cannot be easily concealed. You have disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks and advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks. Magical healing of 6th level or higher removes the scar. | `1d2` weeks |
| 15–20 | **Necrotic Discolouration** | White and grey spots appear on your cheeks. The spots have no adverse effect. Magical healing of 6th level or higher removes them. | — |

## Poison

| d20 | Injury | Description | Length |
|----|----|----|----|
| 1 | **The Long Con** | The poison will kill you in a number of days determined by the Game Master. You gradually discover this as you feel increasingly ill each day. | — |
| 2 | **Microdose** | The poison appears to have helped you slightly. A little more might make you even stronger. | — |
| 3 | **Major Liver Damage** | When you complete a long rest, you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or gain the poisoned condition until you complete another long rest. Whenever you take poison damage, you take an additional `1d6` poison damage. Whenever you drink alcohol or take another drug, you take 3 (`1d6`) poison damage. | `1d4` weeks |
| 4 | **Minor Liver Damage** | When you complete a long rest, you must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain the poisoned condition until you complete another long rest. Whenever you take poison damage, you take an additional `1d6` poison damage. Whenever you drink alcohol or take another drug, you take 3 (`1d6`) poison damage. | `1d4` weeks |

name: Oblate Archaeologist
summary: Character background for a former ruin-delver attuned to the lingering Wild Magic of the Oblate.

fields.languages: Common and one language of your choice

body:
Before becoming an adventurer, you spent much of your early life crawling through dust-filled crypts, abandoned settlements and forgotten ruins in search of relics. Most of your discoveries were of questionable value, but a fortunate few provided enough coin for you to purchase proper adventuring equipment.

One item from those years remains especially important to you.

## Proficiencies

| Category | Proficiencies |
|----|----|
| Skill proficiencies | Perception, Survival |
| Tool proficiencies | [Cartographer's tools](https://5e.tools/items.html#cartographer's%20tools_phb) or [navigator's tools](https://5e.tools/items.html#navigator's%20tools_phb) |
| Languages | Common and one language of your choice |

## Equipment

- A [wooden case](https://5e.tools/items.html#map%20or%20scroll%20case_phb) containing a rough map of the Oblate explosion
- A [bullseye lantern](https://5e.tools/items.html#bullseye%20lantern_phb)
- A [miner's pick](https://5e.tools/items.html#miner's%20pick_phb)
- A set of [traveller's clothes](https://5e.tools/items.html#traveler's%20clothes_phb)
- A [shovel](https://5e.tools/items.html#shovel_phb)
- A [two-person tent](https://5e.tools/items.html#two-person%20tent_phb)
- A vial of acid
- Your signature item

## Signature item

You retained one object from your years exploring crypts and ruins. It may have little practical value, but it carries considerable emotional importance. Roll on the table or choose an item.

| d8 | Signature item |
|----|----|
| 1 | [10-foot pole](https://5e.tools/items.html#pole%20(10-foot)_phb) |
| 2 | Crowbar |
| 3 | Hat |
| 4 | [Hooded lantern](https://5e.tools/items.html#hooded%20lantern_phb) |
| 5 | Medallion |
| 6 | [Hooded lantern](https://5e.tools/items.html#hooded%20lantern_phb) |
| 7 | [Sledgehammer](https://5e.tools/items.html#sledgehammer_phb) |
| 8 | [Whip](https://5e.tools/items.html#whip_phb) |

## Feature: Wild Magic Attunement

Your prolonged exposure to the ruins left by the Oblate has made you unusually sensitive to its lingering influence.

Whenever Wild Magic is cast within one mile of you, you sense its general location.

You can cast *detect magic* at will. When cast in this way, the spell only reveals whether an object, creature or person has been affected by the Oblate. It does not otherwise detect magical auras or reveal their schools of magic.

## GM notes

- The signature-item table lists *Hooded lantern* twice (rows 4 and 6) in every source.

name: Petrification
summary: Progressive petrification that strips an action type each turn until the creature drops to 0 HP and either survives as stone or dies.
body:
At the start of your turn, eliminate one of the following:

- Action
- Bonus Action
- Reaction
- 10 feet of movement

Once you have lost all of these, drop to 0 HP and make death saving throws. If you pass, you are frozen in stone but are alive. If you fail, you become your own grave.

No saves, no mercy.

## How to stop it

- Kill the monster before you transform
- Drink an antidote
- Cast *remove curse*
- Do something clever

name: Sailor (Airship)
summary: Character background for a former airship crew member who can call in favours for free passage.
body:
Before becoming an adventurer, you served aboard one of Kurovia's airships. You may have worked on an Ordonian freight vessel, military patrol craft, passenger liner, exploration ship or independent airship.

Life above the clouds taught you how to work as part of a crew, keep your balance in dangerous conditions and remain alert when open sky lay beneath your feet.

## Proficiencies

| Category | Proficiencies |
|----|----|
| Skill proficiencies | Athletics, Perception |
| Tool proficiencies | [Navigator's tools](https://5e.tools/items.html#navigator's%20tools_phb), [vehicles (air)](https://5e.tools/items.html#blankhash,flstsource:phb=1~dmg=1,flstmiscellaneous:mundane=1,flsttype:vehicle%20(water)=1) |

## Equipment

- 50 feet of rope
- A lucky charm, such as a rabbit foot or a small stone with a hole in the centre (or roll for a random [trinket](https://5e.tools/items.html#trinket_phb))
- A set of [common clothes](https://5e.tools/items.html#common%20clothes_phb)
- A [pouch](https://5e.tools/items.html#pouch_phb) containing 10 gp, or the equivalent value in local currency

## Feature: Airship Passage

When at a major port, you can secure free passage aboard an airship for yourself and your adventuring companions.

The vessel may be an airship on which you previously served, one commanded by a former crewmate, or another craft whose crew owes you a favour.

Because you are relying upon personal connections rather than purchasing ordinary passage, you cannot guarantee that the vessel's route or schedule will perfectly suit your needs. The Dungeon Master determines when an appropriate airship is available, where it is travelling and how long the journey takes.

In exchange for passage, you and your companions are expected to assist the crew during the voyage.

This feature does not guarantee access to military vessels, restricted airspace or destinations considered exceptionally dangerous.

## Airship service

Consider the kind of airship on which you previously served.

| d6 | Former vessel |
|----|----|
| 1 | An Ordonian freight carrier |
| 2 | A military patrol vessel |
| 3 | A passenger airship |
| 4 | A small courier craft |
| 5 | An exploration vessel |
| 6 | An independent vessel |

## Shipboard role

Your former position may help define your duties and relationships aboard the vessel. It does not provide additional proficiencies.

| d8 | Role |
|----|----|
| 1 | Deckhand |
| 2 | Navigator |
| 3 | Engineer's assistant |
| 4 | Lookout |
| 5 | Cargo handler |
| 6 | Gunner |
| 7 | Ship's cook |
| 8 | Cabin attendant |
